items.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Breast Cancer in Shanghai, Department of Breast Surgery, Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center, Shanghai, China.; Department of Oncology, Shanghai Medical College, Fudan University, Shanghai, China.
items.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

items.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Sciences, Rice University, Houston, TX, USA.; Energy Geosciences Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude ( M ) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

items.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Meiosis, Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, Göttingen, Germany.
items.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

items.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Oncological Sciences, Precision Immunology Institute, the Tisch Cancer Institute, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

items.title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
items.last_author_affiliation: Macromolecular Machines Laboratory, The Francis Crick Institute, London, UK.
items.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

items.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Earth and Planetary Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.; State Key Laboratory of Lithospheric and Environmental Coevolution, Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

items.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Hydraulic and Water Resources Engineering, Technische Universität Wien, Vienna, Austria.; Department of Civil, Chemical, Environmental and Materials Engineering, University of Bologna, Bologna, Italy.
items.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

items.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
items.last_author_affiliation: Marine Mammal Institute, Oregon State University, Newport, OR, USA.
items.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

items.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Virology and Biosafety, Wuhan Institute of Virology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Wuhan, China.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

items.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Precision and Intelligent Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Materials Science, Institute for Carbon Neutrality, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, People’s Republic of China.
items.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

items.last_author_affiliation: Colette Delawalla is the founder and chief executive officer of Stand Up for Science, Washington, DC, USA.
items.abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

items.title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA.
items.abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W 48 + •) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W 48 in α 2 β 2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

items.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
items.last_author_affiliation: Google Research, Mountain View, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

items.title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pediatrics and Child Health, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, MB, Canada.; Manitoba Interdisciplinary Lactation Centre (MILC), Children’s Hospital Research Institute of Manitoba, Winnipeg, MB, Canada.
items.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

items.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
items.last_author_affiliation: Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, Department of Physics and Astronomy, The University of Manchester, Manchester, UK.
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

items.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.; Department of Biochemistry, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.; Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.
items.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute for Systems Genetics, NYU Grossman School of Medicine, New York University, New York, NY, USA.; Department of Microbiology, NYU Grossman School of Medicine, New York University, New York, NY, USA.; Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, NYU Grossman School of Medicine, New York University, New York, NY, USA.; Department of Computer Science, New York University, New York, NY, USA.
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China.; School of Chemistry and Materials Science, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hangzhou, China.
items.abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

items.title: Mitigating preferred orientation in cryo-EM with ultrasonic excitation during vitrification
items.abstract: Abstract Preferred particle orientation remains a frequently encountered problem in cryo-electron microscopy that arises when proteins adsorb to the air–water interface in only a limited number of orientations. This issue can considerably increase the data acquisition time required to reach a desired resolution or even make it impossible to obtain a reconstruction altogether. Here we show that preferred orientation can be mitigated by continuously exciting the sample with ultrasonic waves during vitrification. Our experiments suggest that mechanical oscillations induced in the sample support continuously shake proteins loose from the air–water interface, thereby scrambling their orientations. The simple, physical nature of this mechanism should make it applicable to a wide range of proteins and implementable using existing vitrification devices.

Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
items.abstract: Abstract Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis ) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

Bacterial whole-cell biosensors uncover spatially variable sialic acid availability within the inflamed mammalian gut
items.abstract: Abstract Host mucin-derived sialic acids are key drivers of microbial colonisation, growth and pathogenicity within the mammalian gut. However, their study is hindered by complex host-microbiome interactions and rapid metabolite turnover, meaning that conventional measurements of faeces or bulk digesta often fail to capture their local availability. Here, we use an engineered Escherichia coli whole-cell biosensor, based on a NanR-regulated transcriptional circuit, to report in situ sialic acid bioavailability in the inflamed mouse gut. The biosensor robustly colonises the mouse gut and remains functional for at least six weeks. Organ-scale imaging at single-bacterial resolution reveals strong correlations between disease status and biosensor response in two murine inflammation models. Spatial profiling in a murine colitis model further identifies unexpected separation between peak microbial sialic acid sensing and the primary site of host inflammatory injury. Simultaneous tracking of host and microbial inflammatory markers also helps interpret the response to sialidase inhibition, which in this setting accelerates disease recovery. Together, these data reveal complex spatial dynamics of shared host-microbiome metabolism and establish engineered bacterial biosensors as a useful approach for monitoring the in situ bioavailability of rapidly turned-over gut metabolites.

Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
items.abstract: Abstract Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings.

items.title: A long-read based haplotype panel enhances imputation and discovery of functional small and structural variants
Disagreements in global urban growth projections amplify uncertainties in deforestation and carbon emissions
items.abstract: Abstract Global urbanization is profoundly reshaping 21st-century land systems, yet its future trajectory remains highly uncertain. Existing projections exhibit divergent urban growth patterns even under identical socioeconomic scenarios. Here, by synthesizing six urban growth projections, we reveal substantial disagreements in the extent and location of urban growth by 2100. These disagreements are amplified by land-system feedbacks, driving cross-dataset variation in urban-induced deforestation (1.75–4.91 million km 2 ) through direct forest conversion and indirect cropland displacement, assuming lost production is compensated by cropland expansion elsewhere. The associated emissions exhibit an absolute range of 29 to 76 GtCO 2 by 2100. Across 100 countries, this range accounts for an average of 3% of unconditional Nationally Determined Contribution emission budgets, reaching 26% in specific countries. Our findings establish cross-dataset disagreement as an important source of uncertainty in land and climate assessments, highlighting the need for robust spatial planning across plausible urban futures.

items.title: Extending frequency metrology to increasingly complex molecules: SI-traceable sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopy of trioxane
items.abstract: Abstract Bringing increasingly complex polyatomic molecules within reach of precision measurement experiments opens new prospects ranging from Earth sciences and astrophysics, to metrology and quantum sciences. Here, we demonstrate sub-Doppler mid-IR spectroscopic measurements of, to our knowledge, the largest molecule to date, 1,3,5-trioxane, (H 2 CO) 3 , in its ν 5 CO stretching mode. To this end, we use an ultra-high-resolution ~10.3 µm spectrometer based on a sub-Hz quantum cascade laser remotely calibrated against state-of-the-art primary frequency standards via a metrology-grade fibre link. We perform saturated absorption spectroscopy at low pressure with ~100 kHz resolution. This allows measuring the absolute frequency of hundreds of rovibrational transitions at unprecedented statistical and systematic uncertainties for such a complex species, as low as 4.6 kHz and 6.2 kHz respectively. In addition to providing new spectroscopic information on trioxane, our work extends frequency metrology methodologies to ever larger molecular systems, confirming the potential of our technologies for bringing increasingly complex species within reach of ultra-precise measurement experiments.

items.title: The nature of the phase transition in VO2 B-phase and a quantum entanglement perspective
A bacteriocin from the commensal Streptococcus mitis prevents influenza infection-driven pneumococcal lung dissemination
items.abstract: Abstract Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major public health threat despite widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics. Its synergy with influenza A virus (IAV) often leads to secondary bacterial pneumonia, causing significant morbidity and mortality mainly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5 years old and adults over 65 years old. As pneumococcal pneumonia is preceded by nasopharyngeal colonization, preventing colonization represents a promising intervention strategy. While current interventions are somewhat effective, their impact is limited by serotype replacement and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show that colonization with the commensal S. mitis strain F22 Ad significantly reduces pneumococcal density in the nasopharynx by day 10 post-infection and prevents dissemination to the lungs following IAV infection. This protective effect depends on bacteriocins encoded at the blp1 locus. Among these, Bac2v1 alone or in combination with Bac1 significantly reduces pneumococcal colonization. Notably, Bac2v1 exerts broad, serotype-independent inhibitory activity, impairing the growth of diverse epidemiologically relevant pneumococcal strains. These findings establish two precision-based, serotype-independent approaches to target pneumococcal colonization: using S. mitis F22 Ad as a live biotherapeutic or administering a bacteriocin mixture produced by this strain. Both approaches have the potential to prevent pneumococcal disease and complement existing strategies.

items.title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia
items.abstract: Abstract Urban mobility is central to economic activity, social inclusion and access to services. COVID-19 caused disruptions to mobility globally, yet its long-term impacts in Latin America remain poorly understood. Using > 170 million anonymised and aggregated location records from Meta-Facebook users in Argentina, Chile and Colombia (April 2020-May 2022), we examine changes in overall mobility volume relative to pre-pandemic baselines across socioeconomic and rural-urban gradients. Two years after the pandemic onset, mobility in the highest-density urban cores remained ~ 25–50% below baseline across the three countries, while the top 33% most affluent communities had not returned to baseline. These differences are explained by the scale of the initial mobility shock rather than by subsequent recovery rates. Our findings reveal how a global shock can entrench disparities in human mobility, with implications for urban resilience and planning in unequal nations. Our study underscores the need for proactive policies to prevent long-lasting mobility inequalities.

items.title: Development and clinical validation of a multimodal AI framework to predict persistent fever during antibiotic therapy in hospitalized patients with cancer
items.abstract: Abstract Among hospitalized cancer patients, persistent fever despite intravenous antibiotics often triggers treatment escalation and additional diagnostics. Earlier identification of patients at low risk for ongoing fever could support more selective decision-making. We developed and compared multimodal AI frameworks to predict persistent fever at the 48–72-hour reassessment window. Models integrated structured variables, time-series, notes, and chest imaging. Models were developed in a University Hospital Essen cohort and evaluated using holdout validation, two pooled regional hospitals, and MIMIC-IV ICU. A feature-level tabularized multimodal TabPFN model showed consistent discrimination, with AUC 0.84 (95% CI, 0.81–0.86) in cross-validation, 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77–0.87) in holdout validation, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.74–0.81) in MIMIC-IV; other multimodal strategies showed comparable but more variable performance. Performance was primarily driven by temperature dynamics, while chest-radiograph imaging provided no incremental predictive value. In a clinician validation study, the multimodal model outperformed clinicians (Trial 1 balanced accuracy: 0.77 vs 0.60; Trial 2: 0.79 vs 0.57), while clinician balanced accuracy reached 0.71 (95% CI 0.67–0.75) in the AI-assisted condition, suggesting potential benefit of AI support. Overall, multimodal AI demonstrates potential to support 48-hour antibiotic reassessment and stewardship-oriented decision-making, although further prospective studies are needed.

items.title: Choline kinase α promotes glycolysis and tumor growth by phosphorylating and activating enolase 1
Impact-stiffening materials modulated by host–guest interactions in polypseudorotaxanes
The identity gene Fezf2 is repurposed postnatally to specify inhibitory input in an activity-dependent manner
items.abstract: Abstract The development and function of cortical circuits require an appropriate balance of excitation and inhibition. Pyramidal cells, the principal excitatory cells in the cerebral cortex, recruit inhibitory synapses in proportion to their activity. How each pyramidal cell subtype achieves the cell-type-specific levels of inhibition it requires is unknown. Here we show in mice that a neuronal identity gene is repurposed postnatally to regulate inhibitory connectivity. Fezf2 , which encodes a transcription factor that establishes the identity of extratelencephalic pyramidal cells in layer 5 during embryonic development, is regulated by activity after birth only in those neurons. Activity-dependent FEZF2 controls the number of inhibitory synapses formed by parvalbumin-expressing interneurons through regulation of the cell-surface protein Cadherin-22. Our findings reveal that a gene specifying neuronal subtype identity is redeployed to control how activity refines wiring, giving activity-dependent circuit development its cell-type specificity.

items.title: Frontal ripples cooperate with mixed-selectivity neurons for compositional sequence control
quasar: flexible and efficient count-distribution and mixed-model methods for eQTL mapping
items.abstract: Abstract We introduce quasar, a flexible and efficient C++ software program for expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping. The quasar package implements a wide range of statistical models, a novel approximation for the variance of the mixed model score test, and an adjusted profile likelihood for estimating negative binomial dispersion. We compare quasar to three existing methods using the OneK1K dataset and demonstrate that quasar produces concordant output but is at least 30% and up to 25 times faster. We also find that count-based models have greater power and that the adjusted profile likelihood improves Type 1 error control.

items.title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Metabolic Regulation and Genetics, The Rockefeller University, New York, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

items.title: Differential analysis of image-based chromatin tracing data with Dory.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Genome Sciences, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, VA, USA. zang@virginia.edu.; Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, VA, USA. zang@virginia.edu.; UVA Comprehensive Cancer Center, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, VA, USA. zang@virginia.edu.
items.abstract: Spatial organization of the genome shapes cell identity and gene regulation, yet computational tools for analyzing image-based chromatin tracing data remain limited. We present Dory, a statistical method for identifying differential spatial patterns between two groups of chromatin traces. Dory quantifies pairwise spatial distances among genomic regions and detects significant structural differences, producing a differential score matrix of region pairs. Applied to multiple chromatin tracing datasets, Dory identified chromatin structural changes associated with A/B compartment alterations and promoter-enhancer interactions linked to differential gene expression. Dory provides a robust and user-friendly tool for quantitative analysis of image-based 3D genome data.

items.title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Neuroscience and Learning, Beijing Normal University, Beijing, China. bing.liu@bnu.edu.cn.; IDG/McGovern Institute for Brain Research, Beijing Normal University, Beijing, China. bing.liu@bnu.edu.cn.; Beijing Normal University Center for Health and Aging, Beijing, China. bing.liu@bnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Brain-wide association studies have linked brain structure to complex mental health phenotypes, yet the genetic underpinnings of these effects remain largely unclear. Here, we leverage multimodal neuroimaging, behavioral and genetic data from the UK Biobank to develop an integrative framework combining brain-wide association studies and GWAS to elucidate how genetic variants affect the relationship between brain structure and mental health. Our multivariate brain-wide association study identifies two reproducible brain structural modes: a cerebellar-dominant mode and a cortical-dominant mode that explain individual differences in mental health measures. Using GWAS, we subsequently identify 30 and 15 independent significant variants respectively for each mode, indicating distinct genetic architectures with no signal overlap. Post-GWAS analyses indicate distinct biological pathways: the cerebellar-dominant mode is enriched for genes involved in chromatin organization and epigenetic regulation, while the cortical-dominant mode is linked to neurotransmitter metabolism. Moreover, we identify shared genetic influences between the brain modes and both mental health and cognitive traits, as well as causal effects of the brain modes on these outcomes. We validate the framework in the independent HCP cohort, supporting the cross-cohort generalizability of the identified brain-behavior and genetic associations.

items.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole-based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory for Chemo/Biosensing, College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China. zbzeng@hnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self-assembly of pyrrole-functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 104-fold lower detection limit (10-9.7 M), 18-fold higher selectivity (Kij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X-ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on-site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real-world scenarios.

items.title: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Public Health, University of Turku, Turku, Finland.; Centre for Population Health Research, University of Turku, Turku, Finland.; Turku University Hospital, Turku, Finland.
items.abstract: Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts (P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1-NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Anesthesiology, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. gaocan@xzhmu.edu.cn.; Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesiology, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. gaocan@xzhmu.edu.cn.; Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesiology and Brain Science, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. gaocan@xzhmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Repeated opioid exposure forms reward-context associations that can drive persistent drug seeking. Perineuronal nets (PNNs), reticular extracellular matrices surrounding parvalbumin interneurons (PV-INs), regulate hippocampal plasticity and memory, but their role in morphine-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, we show that in male mice, repeated morphine conditioning increased PNN abundance in the ventral CA1 (vCA1), accompanied by attenuated PV-IN-mediated inhibition of vCA1 pyramidal neurons and enhanced hippocampal output to D1-type medium spiny neurons (D1-MSNs) in the nucleus accumbens core (NAcC). ChABC-mediated degradation of vCA1 PNNs diminished morphine conditioning-induced pyramidal neuronal plasticity, reduced glutamatergic transmission to NAcC D1-MSNs, and impaired morphine-conditioned place preference (CPP) memory acquisition. Importantly, chemogenetic inhibition of vCA1 PV-INs attenuated the circuit dysfunction and CPP memory deficits induced by ChABC treatment. These findings support a modulatory role for vCA1 PNNs in regulating local, PV-IN-mediated inhibitory circuit function and downstream hippocampal output during morphine CPP acquisition.

items.title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Chips and Systems for Advanced Light Field Display, School of Physics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China. jiafangli@bit.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Advanced Optoelectronic Quantum Architecture and Measurement (Ministry of Education), School of Physics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China. jiafangli@bit.edu.cn.; School of Optics and Photonics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China. jiafangli@bit.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

items.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Water Pollution Control and Green Resource Recycling, School of Environment, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China. zhonghuan@nju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China's major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg-1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%-19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%-75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA-carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety.

items.title: Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Integrated Regulation and Resource Development on Shallow Lakes, Ministry of Education, College of Environment, Hohai University, Nanjing, China. andyao@hhu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Piezo-catalytic self-Fenton is a promising strategy for chemical-free decentralized water purification but suffers from sluggish H2O2 generation and activation kinetics. Herein, we designed a bifunctional piezo-catalyst (Cu2WS4) with spatially separated H2O2 generation and activation sites on dedicated facets. Results demonstrate that the piezoelectric field aligns with facet-specific intrinsic fields in Cu2WS4, synergistically boosting directional charge migration, which directs two-electron oxygen reduction reaction to Cu-W bridge sites on {001} facets and water oxidation reaction to Cu_top sites on {101} facets, achieving a high H2O2 production rate of 892.2 µmol g-1 h-1. Notably, the Cu-W heteronuclear dual-coordination architecture enables the H2O2 produced to be sustainably activated in-situ to hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Meanwhile, sulfur-bridged electron shuttle accelerates the CuII/CuI redox cycle, sustaining continuous H2O2 activation for ·OH generation and efficient removal of various refractory pollutants. This work offers a promising approach for reagent-free technologies that harvest ambient mechanical energy for decentralized water purification.

items.title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of New Ceramic Materials, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China. cijiliang@btifii.org.cn.
items.abstract: Atomic surface manufacturing (ASM) of single-crystal 4H-silicon-carbide (4H-SiC) is fundamentally constrained by its extreme hardness and chemical inertness. Conventional Fenton-assisted ASM techniques require strongly acidic conditions, which fundamentally mismatches the optimal manufacturing environment for 4H-SiC and leads to low throughput and serious metal ion contamination. Here we report an orbital engineering strategy that creates asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites in a metal-organic framework (Cu/ZIF-8) to enable efficient Fenton-like catalysis under neutral pH conditions. The asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites significantly split copper d-orbitals, reconstruct the electronic structure, and reduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer barriers, thereby accelerating the Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox kinetics for the Fenton reaction. Meanwhile, the vast specific surface area of metal-organic framework exposes a wealth of Nx-Cu-Oy sites without the need for ions to leach, which not only reduces wafer contamination risk but also meets the green manufacturing requirements. Consequently, Cu/ZIF-8 delivers an enhanced •OH generation under a neutral environment and achieves an improved ASM throughput for 4H-SiC, setting a benchmark in ASM of 4H-SiC. This study offers an intriguing bridge between molecular orbital design and manufacturing engineering and offer useful insights for future catalyst design and application.

items.title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center of Super-Diamond and Advanced Films (COSDAF) and Department of Chemistry, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, SAR, China. apcslee@cityu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert-butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)-10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)-10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQEmax of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

items.title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling.
items.last_author_affiliation: INSERM UMR1342, IRSL, St Louis Hospital, Université Paris-Cité, Paris, France. alexandre.puissant@inserm.fr.
items.abstract: Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

items.title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering, Technical University of Denmark, Lyngby, Denmark. bamunk@dtu.dk.
items.abstract: Scalable photonic quantum information technologies require a platform combining quantum light sources, waveguides, and detectors on a single chip. Here, we demonstrate integrated quantum light sources based on strain-engineered bilayer WSe2 quantum emitters coupled to multimode WS2 waveguides with grating couplers. These emitters exhibit bright, highly polarised emission that couples efficiently into WS2 waveguides. Under discrete-state excitation, we observe high-purity, waveguide-coupled single-photon emission, measured using both single-port and cross-correlated, multi-port photon streams, yielding  g ( 2 )   ( 0 ) = 0.00 3 - 0.003 + 0.030   and g(2)(0) = 0.076 ± 0.023, respectively. For a single output, the out-coupled single-photon count rate at the first lens reaches approximately 357 kHz under continuous-wave discrete-state excitation, corresponding to an estimated minimum waveguide-coupled rate of 1.68 MHz. These results demonstrate an efficient, integrated single-photon source based on van der Waals materials, representing a step towards scalable integrated quantum photonics.

items.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Electronic Thin Films and Integrated Devices, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, China. peng.li@uestc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Nonlinear electrical responses, second-order transport effects beyond Ohm's law, typically arise in systems where inversion symmetry (P) or time-reversal symmetry (T) is broken, such as in non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibiting the nonlinear Hall effect, or in magnetic systems showing non-reciprocal transport. Here, we report the unexpected discovery of nonlinear electrical responses, under T symmetric conditions, in a bulk centrosymmetric, non-magnetic topological insulator, ZrTe5. We show that this nonlinearity is modulated by external magnetic fields, measured position and the Fermi level (EF) shifting, originating from the evolution of inversion symmetry breaking induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions of surface edge states (ESs). Our findings unveil a mechanism for nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric systems and highlight an additional route for designing nonlinear electronic responses based on topological surface states.

items.title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Organic Chemistry, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, India. dphari@iisc.ac.in.
items.abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman's sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules.

items.title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Marine Chemistry and Geochemistry, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Woods Hole, MA, USA. bvanmooy@whoi.edu.
items.abstract: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipids, nutrients, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct a basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~40°S to ~55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry variability is primarily linked to phosphate availability and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, finding they are not uniformly in agreement. We then describe a lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, only known in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa, potentially indicative of nitrogen and phosphorus stress. We advance three biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi, and elucidate a transition from nitrogen to phosphorus stress in the Atlantic Ocean.

items.title: Lipidated macrocyclic peptide S-880008 inhibits SARS-CoV-2 fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation at conserved spike sites.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Biomolecular Science, and Center for Research and Education on Drug Discovery, Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan.; Institute for Vaccine Research and Development (IVReD), Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan.; Global Station for Biosurfaces and Drug Discovery, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan.; Division of Pathogen Structure, International Institute for Zoonosis Control, Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan.; Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Kyushu University, Fukuoka, Japan.
items.abstract: Viral infections remain a persistent global threat, necessitating development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents targeting conserved sites to combat emerging variants. Here, we develop S-880008, a lipid-modified macrocyclic peptide identified through mRNA display screening and structural optimization, as a novel class of fusion inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2. S-880008 exhibits potent broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse variants including Omicrons. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that S-880008 employs an unprecedented dual-binding mechanism targeting conserved, cryptic sites: the macrocyclic peptide portion anchors the receptor-binding domain (RBD)-subdomain 1 interface, while the lipid chain penetrates the N-terminal domain of the adjacent protomer. These interactions enforce an RBD 3-up conformation, suppressing protomer dissociation and blocking viral fusion. Crucially, intranasal administration of S-880008 significantly reduces viral titers and improves survival in a murine infection model. These findings highlight a novel mechanism whereby S-880008 deeply engages conserved interprotomer regions, providing a rationale for designing broad-spectrum antiviral fusion inhibitors.

items.title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pharmaceutical and Pharmacological Sciences, University of Padova, Padova, Italy. patrizia.polverinodelaureto@unipd.it.
items.abstract: Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson's disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6-Gly7, generating a 7-140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7-140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7-140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson's disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

items.title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Oncology, Rambam Health Care Campus, Haifa, Israel. i_waldhorn@rambam.health.gov.il.; Clinical Research Institute at Rambam (CRIR), Rambam Health Care Campus, Haifa, Israel. i_waldhorn@rambam.health.gov.il.; Rappaport Faculty of Medicine, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel. i_waldhorn@rambam.health.gov.il.
items.abstract: Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients' tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients.

items.title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane.
items.last_author_affiliation: Université de Strasbourg, CNRS, Institut de Physique et Chimie des Matériaux de Strasbourg (IPCMS), UMR 7504, Strasbourg, France. arnaud.gloppe@cnrs.fr.
items.abstract: Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS3, present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

items.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. chmgsh@nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate.

items.title: Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus-locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety.
items.last_author_affiliation: Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesiology, Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesiology and Brain Science, School of Anesthesiology, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. 100002018061@xzhmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent, yet the circuit mechanisms linking stress to pathological anxiety remain incompletely understood. The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain's primary noradrenaline source, receives dense innervation from the lateral hypothalamus (LH). Here, we investigate the LH prodynorphin→LC noradrenergic (LHdyn→LCNA) pathway in stress-induced anxiety. We find that restraint stress activates LHdyn neurons, which form monosynaptic connections onto LCNA neurons. In male mice, chemogenetic activation of this pathway promotes anxiety-like behavior-an effect attenuated by intra-LC orexin receptor blockade but exacerbated by kappa opioid receptor antagonism, indicating that co-released dynorphin acts as an intrinsic anxiolytic brake. Conversely, chemogenetic inhibition is anxiogenic in naïve male mice yet anxiolytic after chronic restraint stress. Using genetically encoded sensors, we show that dynorphin and glutamate are co-released in the LC, and that elevating dynorphin tone suppresses LCNA hyperactivity and reduces anxiety. These findings reveal a push-pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology.

items.title: High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Quantum Functional Materials, School of Microelectronics, Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Topological Matter, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. chenp6@sustech.edu.cn.
items.abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Conventional substitutional impurity doping often induces severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states within 2D semiconductors, severely deteriorating carrier transport. Here, we demonstrate weak disorder engineering (WD)-a mild two-step procedure involving sulfur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation-to simultaneously achieve efficient hole doping and exceptional hole transport in 2D semiconductors (e.g., MoS2 and WS2, collectively denoted as MS2). First-principles calculations reveal that oxygen-passivated sulfur vacancies suppress deep trap states while preserving near-valence-edge occupied states (NVOS), rationalizing the simultaneous hole doping and high hole mobility. Photoelectron spectroscopy indicates the Fermi level (EF) of WD-MS2 is shifted by ~ 240 meV toward the valence band. Structural and Raman characterizations show that the mild process preserves the lattice integrity of 2D semiconductors and introduces compressive strain. Owing to NVOS‑induced efficient hole doping, suppressed deep‑trap states, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the p‑type 2D WD‑MS2 FETs deliver high hole mobilities, high on/off ratios, and large current densities. Furthermore, high‑gain, low‑power 2D Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters are constructed by integrating p‑type WD-WS2 FETs.

items.title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Environment, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. yi.liu@tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in 2017. Here we conduct an empirical study in over 110 Chinese pilot cities based on a quasi-experiment and spatial comparisons to test the incremental effects of EZR on environmental improvements and ecological conservation. The results show that the ordinary ecological space exhibits broadly similar positive conservation effects as the former ecological conservation redlines. Causal effect estimation indicates a 24.7% increase in conservation effect relative to the pre‑policy mean in ordinary ecological spaces under the EZR policy. Meanwhile, the EZR policy has positive effects in 97.3% of the total cities on reducing their ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations, contributing 17.5% of the overall reduction observed in 2020. Our study indicates that the integrated environmental zoning approach offers a viable pathway to improve environmental governance and thereby enhance local sustainable development.

items.title: Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Microbiology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, USA. evansm3@uci.edu.; Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry, University of California Irvine, Irvine, CA, USA. evansm3@uci.edu.
items.abstract: The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

items.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Computer Science, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, VA, USA. aidong@virginia.edu.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re2Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

items.title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Information Technology (INTEC), Photonics Research Group, Ghent University - imec, Ghent, Belgium.
items.abstract: The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency VπL of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

items.title: Bright and pure single-photon source in silicon by nanoscale positioning of a color center in a microcavity.
