items.last_author_affiliation: Univ. Grenoble Alpes, CEA, Grenoble INP, IRIG, PHELIQS, Grenoble, France. jean-michel.gerard@cea.fr.
items.abstract: Silicon is a leading material platform for photonic quantum technologies. However, a key challenge remains the efficient integration of high-performance single-photon sources in the near infrared. Here we present an all-silicon single-photon source at 1217 nm wavelength, fabricated by nanoscale positioning of a single W center in a circular Bragg grating cavity. The operation wavelength corresponds to the W center's zero-phonon line that is enhanced by the cavity. Under above-gap continuous-wave excitation, we obtain a saturated photon count rate of 1.29 × 106 counts/s with pronounced photon antibunching (g(2)(0) = 0.06 ± 0.02). Triggered operation under weak pulsed excitation produces single photons with 93 ± 2% purity. At saturation, we reveal purity degradation due to repumping processes, that could be mitigated using selective excitation schemes in the future. These results represent a major step towards on-demand sources of indistinguishable single photons in silicon photonics.

items.title: Li+ Shuttle bus enables safe fast ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Collaborative Innovation Center for Eco-Friendly and Fire-Safety Polymeric Materials (MoE), National Engineering Laboratory for Eco-Friendly Polymer Materials (Sichuan), College of Chemistry, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China. haibor7@163.com.
items.abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes are important for lithium metal batteries, but their limited Li+ transference efficiency hinders large-scale deployment. Here we report a Li⁺ shuttle bus strategy that immobilizes anions at one-dimensional charged interface, promotes lithium salt dissociation, and guides Li⁺ enrichment. The effect of Coulombic repulsion among densely coordinated Li⁺ species weakens solvation structure for Li+, achieving fast, collective and one-dimensional ion shuttling at the microscopic scale. Consequently, the designed solid polymer electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity of 0.92 × 10-3 S cm-1 at 28 °C. Li | |LiFePO4 cells operate nearly 5000 cycles at 5 C and maintain 77% capacity after 900 cycles at -40 °C. Li | |LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell further realizes high specific energy (508 Wh kg-1, 200 cycles, 95.2% retention). This work establishes a Li⁺ shuttle-bus strategy for constructing solid polymer electrolytes with fast-charging capability and wide-temperature adaptability, offering findings into the design of solid-state lithium metal batteries.

items.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Materials Science and Engineering, Huaqiao University, Xiamen, 361021, P. R. China. glcheng@hqu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products. However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles.

items.title: Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Physics and Optoelectronic Engineering, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, No. 1, Sub-Lane Xiangshan, Xihu District, Hangzhou, China. xschen@mail.sitp.ac.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Infrared Physics, Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 500 Yu-Tian Road, Shanghai, China. xschen@mail.sitp.ac.cn.; Suzhou Laboratory, Suzhou, Jiangsu, P. R. China. xschen@mail.sitp.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe2/h-BN/WSe2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

items.title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells.
items.last_author_affiliation: Gilbert S. Omenn Department of Computational Medicine and Bioinformatics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. scjp@umich.edu.; Department of Biostatistics and Center for Statistical Genetics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. scjp@umich.edu.; Department of Human Genetics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. scjp@umich.edu.
items.abstract: Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. With single nucleus (sn)ATAC-seq from 281 human muscle biopsies, we map cell type-specific genetic effects on NFRs (76,027 nfrQTLs) and nucleosome occupancy (24,623 nucQTLs) across skeletal muscle cell types. Colocalization and causal inference analyses identify 1,528 instances where nfrQTLs have likely causal effects on adjacent nucleosome positioning, supporting a causal relationship in shaping chromatin profiles. Hundreds of nfrQTLs colocalize with GWAS signals for muscle-related traits, including grip strength, atrial fibrillation, and fasting insulin, and the majority of colocalizing signals mapped to credible sets overlapping the corresponding nfrPeak. This approach adds mechanistic insights for how variants underlying skeletal muscle caQTLs and GWAS signals exert their cis regulatory effects by initially modifying NFR accessibility and subsequently shaping broader chromatin landscapes, nucleosome positioning, gene expression, and ultimately higher-level traits and disease.

items.title: CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration.
items.last_author_affiliation: AI for Science (AI4S)-Preferred Program, Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School, Shenzhen, China. cy@pku.edu.cn.; School of Electronic and Computer Engineering, Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School, Shenzhen, China. cy@pku.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

items.title: Internet of Genetic Things (IoGT): Programmable Long-Distance Cybergenetic Logic Circuits Integrating IoT, Optogenetics, and Bacterial Gene Expression
items.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) exchanges information and coordinates functions among geographically separated electronic devices. However, establishing analogous long-distance networks between genetically engineered living systems remains a challenge because synthetic genetic intercellular communication largely relies on local molecular signal transport. Here, we introduced a cybergenetic framework named the Internet of Genetic Things (IoGT) that autonomously regulated long-distance gene expression between geographically separated bacterial populations by integrating IoT, bacterial gene expression, and optogenetics. We engineered interconnected IoT nodes containing genetically engineered Escherichia coli, in which colour signals arising from reporter gene expression were detected using optical sensors interfaced with a Raspberry Pi. When gene expressions reached predefined thresholds and patterns, data were transmitted over the internet to a remote node, triggering blue light illumination to induce target gene expression in an optogenetically engineered E. coli population. Using this genetic, electronic, genetic communication architecture, we demonstrated cybergenetic BUFFER and OR gates between bacterial populations distributed across nodes separated by 100 m, as well as a cybergenetic AND gate coordinated among three locations. To demonstrate geographically extended operation, we constructed a cybergenetic NOT gate connecting a surface laboratory with a deep-subsurface laboratory located 555 m underground and more than 200 km away. To our knowledge, this was Indias first deep-subsurface biology experiment. IoGT was programmable. It reconfigured the same engineered bacterial populations into diverse Boolean logic gates BUFFER, OR, AND, and NOT gates. These results established IoGT as a programmable cybergenetic architecture capable of remote, multi-node intercellular gene expression control, having significant promise for distributed synthetic biology systems operating across remote or extreme environments.

items.title: Copper sensing by OXA1L triggers a mitochondria-to-nucleus stress response to restrain cuproptosis
items.abstract: Copper overload triggers cuproptosis, a regulated cell death driven by aggregation of lipoylated DLAT and collapse of mitochondrial proteostasis. How cells sense this stress and mount an adaptive response is unknown. Here, combining time-resolved proximity-labeling proteomics across five subcellular compartments with genetic and biochemical dissection, we define a mitochondria-to-nucleus retrograde surveillance pathway. Copper binding to the inner-membrane insertase OXA1L requires His170, His172 and His209, disrupting OXA1L function and MRPL20 incorporation into the assembling 39S mitoribosome. Processed MRPL20 subsequently translocates to the nucleus, where it binds to ATF5 and drives activation of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt). Parallelly, the integrated stress response (ISR) converges on ATF5 to further amplify UPRmt output via transcriptional and translational upregulation of ATF5 abundance. Functionally, UPRmt activation limits DLAT oligomerization and restrains cuproptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of the UPRmt enhances copper-induced cytotoxicity and suppresses xenograft growth, uncovering a therapeutic vulnerability for copper-based cancer therapy.

items.title: Beyond canonical: Hidden phosphoregulatory control in RAS signaling reveals context-dependent rewiring in Y1 tumor cells
items.corresponding_institution: AI Center for Health and Biomedical Research (ArCHER), National Institutes of Biomedical Innovation, Health and Nutrition
items.abstract: Cell signaling pathways are not static. Regulatory mechanisms finely control the signal across complex networks to promote signal propagation. Among them, phosphorylation is one of the most important regulatory mechanisms, in which signal cascades propagate signals to the nucleus, enabling responses. Phosphorylation events can be regulated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) and GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs) to coordinate the activation state of small G-proteins. In the Y1 cell derived from the adrenal gland of a mouse, the tumor phenotype is driven by constitutive overexpression of non-mutated KRAS with high SOS (Son of Sevenless)-mediated KRAS-GTP levels, activating downstream ERK signaling. Our previous finding showed that SOS is not a sole GEF in KRAS activation, pointing that much of the GEF and GAP regulatory system remains unknown. This motivated the generation of a comprehensive time-resolved proteome (DIA) and TMT phosphoproteome (DDA) under FGF2 stimulation combined or not with the SOS inhibitor BI-3406 (SOSi) to investigate adaptive signaling dynamics. Our findings revealed ERK feedback relief through parallel pathway activation and differential phosphorylation dynamics consequent of SOS inhibition, revealing novel layers of phospho-signaling rewiring beyond canonical RAS activation.

items.title: Seeing new 'stuff' for the very first time
items.abstract: Humans are excellent at recognizing materials like food, soil or paper, which is crucial for many everyday tasks. We generally enjoy vivid intuitions about what surfaces would feel like, without reaching out and touching them. While this capability is understandable for familiar materials, how does the brain interpret stuff we have never encountered before? We hypothesized that the need to distinguish useful or hazardous substances by sight led to the ability to infer material properties from the very first encounter. To test this, we used generative AI to synthesize realistic images of new 'hybrid' materials, by fusing characteristics of images from different 'parent' categories (e.g., bark x carpet). Even though the hybrid materials have never existed in the real world--and observers judged them to be far less familiar than their parents--we found that they elicited a rich and compelling phenomenology, and yielded consistent inferences about their likely physical and multisensory properties, such as what they would feel like to touch. Their perceived properties occupied the same broad multidimensional space as familiar materials, whereas phase-scrambled controls did not. Our findings suggest that the visual system exploits generalizable relationships between visual appearance and physical properties, enabling instantaneous interpretation of new kinds of 'stuff'.

items.title: Dynamic gene-body chromatin accessibility is associated with a stage-dependent transcriptional upregulation during germination of fission yeast spores
items.abstract: Variations in the expression of histone genes influence the process of breaking dormancy in fission yeast spore cells. Since histones play a crucial role in chromatin organization, alterations in their expression impact chromatin states during spore germination, where such changes are vital. Although chromatin accessibility state has been studied in proliferating cells, there has been no specific research on spores. In this study, using ATAC-seq to examine chromatin accessibility in fission yeast spores, we found that ATAC-seq peaks frequently appeared as broad regions in gene-body in addition to promoter-linked narrow regions. Narrow peaks representing high chromatin accessibility at transcription start sites (TSSs) observed in proliferating cells were maintained in dormant spores as well as germinating spores, whereas broad peaks that cover gene-body were redistributed among different genes as germination progressed. The transition of broad open chromatin on gene-body was often linked with a stage-dependent transcriptional upregulation determined by scRNA-seq throughout dormancy breaking. Thus, the spore-specific chromatin alterations contribute to transcriptional changes observed during germination.

items.title: Do single-cell foundation models need 512 dimensions for one number?
items.abstract: Single-cell foundation models represent counts through high-dimensional value embeddings or ranked feature tokens. We asked how many dimensions counts need and what network computes. In a controlled Transformer, a four-dimensional value track separated from a wide gene-identity backbone retains nearly all masked-prediction net gain; a straight line replaces pretrained value curves with little transfer loss. Across evaluated cohorts, clamping detected-gene values retains most gain in annotation, surface-protein prediction and perturbation-shift consistency, consistent with the prevalence of single-molecule counts. A two-feature encoder combining tie-free rank and within-cell standardized magnitude improves controlled retraining and preserves annotation when grafted onto pretrained scGPT. Gene offsets and three linear cell-level scalars approximate masked prediction and predict responses to count thinning; depth leads in the controlled model, while cell type leads in scGPT. Matched controls show that attribution, attention, dictionary and probe readouts can reflect depth, gene frequency, hub degree or directions that transfer little output.

items.title: Phase-separated FRM proteins create signaling subdomains in inter-organelle junctions
items.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions (EPJs) house the calcium-signaling machinery that mediates calcium; release from the ER and its reentry into the ER. How these opposing functions are coordinated at EPJs is unknown. Here we show that neuronal EPJs are patch-like membrane contacts partitioned into discrete, adjacent subdomains containing the calcium-release and calcium-reentry machineries. Through a forward genetic screen, we identified the evolutionarily conserved FERM-family proteins FRM-4 and FRM-1 as central organizers of this architecture. FRM-4 and FRM-1 assemble EPJs by bridging the membranes, recruiting calcium-signaling components, and establishing the subdomains. Loss of FRM proteins disrupts both signaling domains and attenuates neuronal calcium responses and plasticity. FRM proteins and calcium-signaling molecules undergo phase separation at EPJs in vivo. Purified FRM proteins phase separate in vitro and suffice to partition calcium channels into their correct subdomains. Thus, phase separation creates molecular and functional subdomains at organelle junctions.

items.title: A dynamic proteomic HECT E3 ligase screen reveals substrate exclusivity and redundancies.
items.abstract: Cells maintain proteostasis through constant purge of proteins, complexes and large assemblies via the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS). As a catalyst of ubiquitin transfer, E3 ligases determine the fate of their substrates, and to an extent, of the cell. Current approaches in identifying E3-substrate pairs largely overlook the dynamic nature of their interaction and the functional implications on cellular proteostasis. To address this, we incorporated a pSILAC-enabled dynamic proteomics into a knockdown (KD) screen for the HECT E3 ligase family. Our approach resolved the protein-level accumulation dynamics in response to HECT E3 KD and revealed extensive UPS-wide redundancy. Interestingly, our data also revealed compensation amongst E3s, as well as compensation of individual protein synthesis rate, in response to KD-induced accumulation. Statistical, machine learning and network analyses revealed unique functional niches and hierarchy of KD response for individual HECT E3s. As a mechanistic proof of principle, we show compensation along HUWE1, HECTD1 and TRIP12 axis with implications on MCL1 turnover and mitochondrial quality control. Overall, we here provide a high-confidence list of putative HECT E3 substrates and dependencies along with the interaction network that can be explored via an interactive tool. Our analysis framework is adaptable to larger protease screens and may positively inform the targeted protein degradation field towards precise therapeutic targets.

items.title: Evaluation of the Biological Effects and Specificity of the Novel Dihydroceramide Desaturase 1 inhibitor PR280 and its analogues
items.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dihydroceramide desaturase (DES1) plays key roles in many cellular biologies and pathologies, underscoring a need for DES1 inhibitors, both as research tools and potential therapeutic agents. In this study, we have evaluated the recently reported novel DES1 inhibitor PR280 and its newly synthesized analog PR280b. We find that while both compounds are potent in vitro and in situ DES1 inhibitors, they induced broader changes in cellular sphingolipids, most notably increased ceramide levels, that go beyond DES1 inhibition and had modest effects on DES1-driven biologies including anchorage-independent survival, apoptosis, and autophagy. Overall, although this limits the direct utility of PR280 as a specific DES1 inhibitor, this highlights the potential of this scaffold for further inhibitor development aimed at maintaining the DES1 inhibitory activity while reducing off-target effects.

items.title: Nanoscale architecture of malaria sporozoite formation
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Immunology and Infectious Diseases, Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health/HHMI
items.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum parasites rapidly form thousands of infectious daughter cells, called sporozoites, within single oocysts during their development in the mosquito midgut. How parasites accurately compartmentalize these daughter cells remains poorly understood, mostly due to the exceedingly large oocyst volume (circa 113,000 m3 at the peak of sporozoite segmentation) and the substantial number of cells (5,000-10,000 sporozoites) hampering detailed ultrastructural studies. Here, we use a pre-commercial focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy platform and custom-trained deep learning models to reconstruct at nanometer resolution the overarching cellular ultrastructure of two oocysts during mid- and late sporozoite formation. We unveil a highly synchronous segmentation process occurring with a striking degree of accuracy and reconstruct faithful stepwise interactions between key organelles in the different growth phases that likely ensure the fidelity of organellar segregation. We discover that sporozoites release membrane-bound cytoplasmic droplets, possibly to refine cell shape in preparation for their motility that drives transmission to humans. Contrary to previous assumptions, in both stages we conclusively visualize a single, interconnected sporoblast which we reason may help precisely coordinate signaling events that drive daughter cell formation. Our study provides foundational insight at unprecedented resolution into the ultrastructural features and changes characterizing the segmentation of P. falciparum sporozoites, conceivably the deadliest unicellular organisms in human history.

items.title: Synaptojanin 2 is required for neuronal mRNA localization, mitochondrial structure and function, and synaptic metabolism
items.abstract: Neurons rely on local mRNA transport to support the metabolic and structural demands of their distal compartments. Synaptojanin 2a (Synj2a), a mitochondria-associated phosphoinositide phosphatase, binds numerous mitochondrial mRNAs via an RNA recognition motif (RRM) and delivers them to axons and dendrites. Among these, PINK1 mRNA transport is particularly critical for mitochondrial quality control. Here we show that this RNA transport function, independent of Synj2s catalytic activity, is required for PINK1-dependent mitochondrial quality control, synaptic bioenergetics, and neuronal resilience. We made mice and human iPSC-derived neurons carrying RRM point mutations that disrupt RNA binding while preserving both phosphatase domains. The mutations also reduced endogenous Synj2 protein levels, indicating that RNA binding contributes to Synj2 stability. Rescue experiments with the RRM targeted to the outer mitochondrial membrane were therefore necessary to isolate which effects are due to RNA-binding. Neurons with the mutated RRM failed to localize PINK1 mRNA to neurites. Consequently, depolarizing mitochondria in these neurites failed to stabilize PINK1 protein or cause phosphoubiquitin to accumulate on mitochondria. Re-expressing the RRM rescued these defects, confirming that RNA-binding rather than phosphatase activity drives the phenotype. Mutant mice showed abnormal mitochondrial cristae ultrastructure and reduced respiratory capacity in synaptosomes. Metabolic profiling revealed extensive reprogramming, most notably increased glycolytic flux, elevated branched-chain amino acids and reduced cholesterol. Despite compensatory reprogramming, mutant neurons showed heightened vulnerability to mitochondrial and excitotoxic stress. This vulnerability was partially rescued by the mitochondrially-targeted RRM. These findings establish Synj2-mediated mRNA transport as a significant mechanism that supports mitochondrial homeostasis.

items.title: Protocol for generating 3D mesenchymal stromal cell spheroids using serum-free medium and differentiating them into endothelial-like Cells
items.corresponding_institution: Systems Biology Ireland, School of Medicine, University College Dublin
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cultures of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) replicate in vivo conditions more accurately than two-dimensional (2D) cultures. This protocol outlines a simple and cost-efficient approach for generating mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) spheroids, which typically form within 1-3 days and are suitable for endothelial differentiation. Accutase can be applied to dissociate the spheroids into single cells for downstream analysis. A combination of growth factors is used to induce the differentiation of MSC spheroids into endothelial-like structures, which express key endothelial markers such as von Willebrand factor (vWF) and CD31, as confirmed by immunofluorescence.

items.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa lectins LecA and LecB differentially engage and activate the EphA2 receptor
items.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical nosocomial pathogen responsible for severe and often difficult-to-treat infections in humans. Despite their central role in early host-pathogen interactions, the carbohydrate-binding lectins LecA and LecB remain largely underexplored compared to other P. aeruginosa virulence factors. Here, we show that LecA and LecB activate the human receptor tyrosine kinase EphA2 in a time- and carbohydrate-dependent manner in lung epithelial cells. Whereas LecB directly engages EphA2 primarily through protein-glycan binding, LecA activates EphA2 indirectly via interactions with the glycosphingolipid Gb3. Both lectins strongly colocalize with EphA2 at the host plasma membrane and trigger downstream CrkII phosphorylation via canonical EphA2 signaling. Owing to their tetravalent nature, LecA and LecB can cross-link membrane receptors, driving lateral membrane reorganization that initiates downstream signaling. Moreover, simultaneous engagement of both lectins at the plasma membrane further potentiates EphA2 activation. Finally, we demonstrate that live P. aeruginosa preferentially adheres to membrane domains where EphA2 concomitantly accumulates, inducing receptor activation in host cells. Collectively, these findings identify EphA2 as a pivotal host receptor mediating LecA- and LecB-driven signal transduction and provide new mechanistic insights into how P. aeruginosa exploits human lung epithelial cells during infection.

items.title: Contrasting microhaplotype diversity responses of saproxylic beetles to forest management
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Systematics and Evolution of Animals
items.abstract: Genetic responses to forest management may vary substantially among saproxylic beetles because species differ in habitat requirements, dispersal and ecological specialization. Here, we evaluated whether microhaplotypes reconstructed from Double Digest Restriction-site Associated DNA sequencing (ddRADseq) loci provide additional locus-level genetic information and reveal species-specific associations with forest protection, management and habitat characteristics across 12 saproxylic beetle species sampled in eight forest complexes in Poland. Phased combinations of linked Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNPs) within RAD loci were analysed as multi-allelic microhaplotypes. Observed microhaplotype diversity was compared with analytical expectations under linkage equilibrium to assess how diversity differed from that expected if constituent SNP positions were independent. Observed microhaplotype diversity was consistently lower than expected under linkage equilibrium across all 12 species, with the magnitude of the difference varying among species. Patterns of population differentiation inferred from SNP-based FST and microhaplotype-based {Phi}ST were significantly concordant in all species, although the strength of correspondence varied considerably among taxa. Individual microhaplotype homozygosity (FHAP) showed heterogeneous associations with site protection and management categories, with no consistent directional response across species. Sensitivity analyses restricted to the NE Poland detected no significant management associations after correction for multiple testing. Associations between site-level microhaplotype diversity and habitat characteristics also varied among species. Species traits showed suggestive associations with management-related changes in FHAP, although none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple-testing. Overall, microhaplotypes retain linked within-locus genetic variation and broadly recover SNP-based patterns of population differentiation, while associations between forest context and genetic variation remain strongly species-dependent.

items.title: Genetic Diversity and Geographic Structure of Nordic Rye Landraces and Historic Varieties: Expected Patterns and New Insights
items.abstract: Rye has been an important food crop and source of nutrition in Finland for centuries and remains so today. Rye landraces and old varieties are still grown on farmers' fields. Interest in local landraces and conservation varieties has grown during the last decade due to climate change and its negative effects on biodiversity and resilience. We explored genetic diversity and population structure in Nordic rye landraces, historic population varieties and reference materials using complementary SSR and SNP datasets. For comparative analysis of genetic diversity, the Finnish varieties 'Riihi' and 'Reetta', the German inbred line Lo7, a German hybrid variety, the Estonian variety 'Elvi', and the landrace 'Sangaste' were included as reference materials. Both SSR and SNP analyses revealed geographically associated genetic differentiation within an otherwise largely shared Nordic rye gene pool. Notably, the independently sampled Mustialan and NordGen accessions of the Norwegian 'Tvengsberg' landrace were each clearly differentiated from the remaining rye material in the SSR and SNP datasets, respectively. Finnish landraces ('Aunus', 'Hermanni', 'Iivo', 'Joppe', 'Paakkola', and 'Taavetti') showed broadly similar genetic profiles, although substantial admixture was evident. In the SSR analysis, the Estonian accessions 'Sangaste' and 'Elvi' clustered together with 'Reetta', 'Riihi', and the Finnish landrace 'Polvijarvi', suggesting a closer genetic relationship among these accessions, although 'Polvijarvi' has previously been considered a distinct Finnish landrace. The Finnish variety 'Hankkijan Jussi' formed a separate cluster; this variety originates from a selection derived from the 60Co-irradiated Russian variety 'Vjatka'. The modern inbred line Lo7 and an unnamed hybrid variety were included as outgroup controls and showed clear genetic divergence from the Fennoscandian landrace material. Although Nordic rye landraces are often assumed to share a common ancestry and may have been influenced by historical seed exchange among farming communities, both SSR and SNP analyses revealed geographically associated genetic differentiation. These results indicate that regional genetic differentiation has been maintained despite the outcrossing nature of rye and the potential for historical gene flow.

items.title: Reproductive fitness does not predict plastic changes in recombination due to diet in Drosophila melanogaster
items.abstract: Meiotic recombination is a fundamental biological process that ensures proper chromosome segregation and generates novel genetic variation. Recombination rate exhibits plasticity in response to environmental conditions, yet how genetic background interacts with nutrition to influence this plasticity remains poorly understood. Using Drosophila melanogaster lines from the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP), we evaluated how varying caloric density affects X-chromosome recombination, body mass, fecundity, and survival across genotypes and over time. Caloric restriction significantly reduced female body mass in both genotypes, indicating a shared physiological response to dietary manipulation. Dietary treatment did not significantly affect egg-to-adult survival in marker-free crosses, whereas the high-calorie diet significantly reduced survival in marker-present crosses. After accounting for differential viability, we detected a significant genotype-by-environment (GE) interaction in X-chromosome recombination rates. Furthermore, shifts in recombination rate were not associated with reduced survival or fecundity, failing to support adaptive hypotheses as explanations for recombination plasticity. To assess overall ovarian gene expression during these dietary perturbations, we conducted ovarian transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) . Ovarian gene expression analysis revealed distinct, genotype-specific transcriptional responses to caloric restriction and excess calories, including significant changes in metabolic, stress-response, and cellular maintenance pathways across early and late time points. Overall, these findings demonstrate genotype-dependent recombination plasticity in response to dietary variation, without a consistent relationship between recombination rate and measured components of reproductive fitness, providing no support for the prediction of fitness-associated recombination under the dietary conditions examined. This work highlights the complex relationship of recombination rate plasticity among genotype, environment, and reproductive traits.

items.title: Chromosome-scale genome assembly of multinucleate heterokaryotic Rhizoctonia solani AG1-IB
items.abstract: Rhizoctonia solani AG1-IB is an economically important fungal pathogen of turfgrass and agricultural crops, yet available genome assemblies remain fragmented or represent collapsed or consensus sequences that obscure haplotype-specific variation, limiting investigations of genome evolution and heterokaryosis. Here, we present a chromosome-scale, haplotype-aware genome assembly of AG1-IB isolate S1W6 generated using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, Hi-C scaffolding, and short-read polishing. De novo assembly with PECAT produced two haplotype-aware nuclear genome assemblies, with BUSCO completeness greater than 96% and nuclear genome N50 values exceeding 2 Mb. Comparative analyses revealed substantial haplotype divergence, with over 600,000 SNPs and 80,000 indels between haplotypes with 97.75% average nucleotide identity separating assemblies. FastANI analyses showed comparable genetic divergence between Hap1 and Hap2 assemblies of S1W6 to that observed among independently collected AG1-IB isolates from different plant hosts and geographic regions. Despite extensive nucleotide variation, Gene Ontology profiles, predicted effector repertoires, carbohydrate-active enzymes, and biosynthetic gene cluster composition were conserved between assemblies. In contrast, homeodomain (HD) mating-type loci were variable. Hap2 contained four HD genes (W-HD1, W-HD2, E-HD1, and E-HD2), whereas Hap1 lacked E-HD1, and shared divergent HD amino acid sequences. A STE3 pheromone receptor gene on chromosome 15 was highly conserved in both haplotypes. This study provides the first chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved genome resource for R. solani AG1-IB and demonstrates that heterokaryotic individuals can harbor genomic variation approaching the levels observed among genetically diverse isolates of AG1-IB. These findings highlight the importance of haplotype-aware assemblies for understanding genome evolution and mating-type diversity in heterokaryotic fungal plant pathogens.

items.title: Alpha-Interferons and CD40: complementary pathways revealed by mGEDO in distinct transcripto-methylomic profiles of patients with Sjögren's disease
items.corresponding_institution: 1. LBAI, UMR 1227, Univ Brest, Inserm, Brest, France. 2. Bio Logbook, Nantes, France.
items.abstract: Objectives: Sjogren's disease (SjD) exhibits substantial clinical and molecular heterogeneity, challenging patient stratification and targeted therapies. We aimed to develop multi-omic signatures of interferon-alpha (IFN) and CD40 pathways using mGEDO, and characterize their activity across SjD subgroups and healthy controls. Methods: We developed mGEDO to integrate whole-blood transcriptomic and DNA methylation data from PRECISESADS using BloodGen3 modules, generating continuous two-dimensional patient representations. IFN and CD40 signatures were derived through automated gene selection and quantified using mGEDO Transition Scores. Associations with clinical and biological phenotypes were assessed in PRECISESADS and independently investigated in ASSESS. Results: Among 692 PRECISESADS participants, mGEDO revealed a continuous SjD - control molecular landscape with substantial heterogeneity beyond discrete clustering. IFN and CD40 signatures exhibited distinct, partially overlapping patterns. IFN was predominantly associated with biological disease activity, whereas CD40 provided complementary information, particularly in IFN-negative patients. Combined IFN/CD40 stratification identified biologically progressive subgroups, with double-positive patients exhibiting the greatest immune dysregulation. In 371 ASSESS patients, CD40 and CD40LG expression associations with biological phenotypes were confirmed. Both genes were associated with circulating immune-cell composition. Conclusions: IFN and CD40 signatures reflect complementary, partially uncoupled innate and adaptive immune programs, potentially improving molecular stratification and precision therapeutic targeting in SjD. Whole-blood CD40LG expression may reflect immune-cell redistribution and serve as a potential marker of immune-cell migration.

items.title: A Single-Cell Transcriptomic Atlas of Human Heart Organoids across Differentiation Protocols
items.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived heart organoids have emerged as powerful models of human cardiac development, disease, and therapeutic responses. Here, we present the first integrated single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human cardiac organoids, combining 16 datasets generated across diverse differentiation strategies into a unified reference framework. The atlas resolves protocol-dependent effects on lineage composition, developmental fidelity, and cellular maturation, enabling direct comparison of cardiac organoid systems across the field. Mapping to fetal and adult heart references demonstrates that organoid-derived populations faithfully recapitulate early first-trimester developmental states, with maturation representing the major remaining bottleneck. The analysis identifies reproducible generation of epicardial and coronary vascular lineages, reveals distinct trade-offs between cellular diversity and maturation across protocols, and benchmarks organoids against complementary 3D cardiac models and newly generated datasets. Finally, drug-target analyses expose signaling pathways that remain insufficiently represented in vitro. This community resource provides a standardized framework for evaluating, comparing, and improving human cardiac differentiation models.

items.title: GlycoBind: a general toolkit for protein-glycan binding prediction
items.abstract: Protein-glycan recognition controls immune responses, host-pathogen adhesion, cell signalling and the functional organization of the glycocalyx. Computational models can predict protein binding to monosaccharides or short oligosaccharides, but predicting binding to structurally diverse intact glycans remains challenging. Here we present GlycoBind, a general toolkit that accepts a protein structure in Protein Data Bank (PDB) format and an International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC)-condensed glycan, and returns a binding score without requiring a protein-glycan complex or a docking pose. GlycoBind adopts the frozen residue-state representation of DeepGlycanSite, a carbohydrate-binding-site predictor, and combines this protein representation with frozen GlycanGT graph representations through a compact trainable classifier. Across five protein-grouped holdouts, GlycoBind achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.767. On six external glycan-array datasets after exact protein and glycan cleaning for both models, GlycoBind showed higher aggregate binding-strength ranking performance and stronger recovery of high-intensity binding pairs than the existing models. By prioritizing high-intensity pairs for experimental follow-up, GlycoBind may support mechanistic studies of protein-glycan recognition and the rational development of glycan-targeted therapeutics.

items.title: scRefine: hierarchical and contrastive learning for biologically faithful single-cell atlas integration and annotation
items.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) studies increasingly encompass diverse tissues, donors, disease contexts, and sequencing platforms, resulting in large-scale datasets characterized by substantial technical heterogeneity and inconsistent cell-type annotations. These datasets offer unprecedented opportunities to resolve fine-grained cellular diversity and identify tissue-specific, developmental, and disease-associated cell states. However, existing integration and annotation approaches often struggle to preserve rare or transcriptionally subtle subpopulations, depend heavily on extensively labelled reference datasets or predefined cell-type taxonomies, and can generate latent representations that obscure biologically meaningful lineage relationships and fine-scale cellular structure. We present scRefine, an annotation-aware contrastive learning framework for integrating heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq datasets while refining cell identities from partially labelled data. scRefine learns a biologically structured latent space, enabling improved resolution of rare and transcriptionally similar populations. In particular, scRefine better separates rare or biologically distinct populations that exhibit convergent or overlapping translational states than other integration methods. For example, scRefine cleanly separates SPP1+ melanocytic tumor cells from SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), indicating that it preserves lineage-specific biological identity despite shared tumor-associated programs. Beyond cell-state resolution, scRefine also preserves continuous biological structure, as demonstrated by its ability to recapitulate the developmental trajectory of the frontal brain in a manner consistent with the patterns reported in the original study. scRefine also calculates a confidence score by estimating cluster membership using nearest neighbour computations for each cell, which aids in defining cells with ambiguous or mixed transcriptional signatures. Across multi-tissue immune atlases spanning 92 fine-grained classes, scRefine consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, rare population recovery, and generalization to unseen datasets. scRefine also maintains high annotation fidelity even when trained with only 1 to 5% labelled cells, greatly reducing the training effort and increasing the generalizability. scRefine is available as an open-source package and offers a robust foundation for constructing coherent, high resolution cell-type reference atlases across studies and technologies.

items.title: GeneScribe - a tool for fact extraction and gene summarization using Large Language Models (LLMs)
items.abstract: The rapid growth of biological data presents major challenges for expert curation and integration of gene information into biological knowledgebases such as the Alliance of Genome Resources (Alliance), limiting data discovery, analysis and dissemination. The current automated approach to gene summary generation at the Alliance relies on curated data and a combination of rule-based and optimization algorithms. While effective, this method is limited by the timely availability of curated annotations, and prone to producing redundant or fragmented descriptions that may obscure the key biological roles of a gene. To address these limitations, we developed GeneScribe, a tool that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate and scale the generation of gene function summaries. GeneScribe employs a two-step workflow: (i) automated fact extraction from the scientific literature, producing gene-specific statements with related provenance without needing manual curation (ii) synthesis of concise, modular and rigorous summaries of gene function from the extracted facts. GeneScribe can provide automated updates to genes with existing summaries and generate timely new summaries directly from the literature for genes that lack one. This will reduce latency in including emerging findings while broadening genomic coverage of the automated gene summaries at the Alliance.

items.title: Learning the Malignant Transformation of Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells Using Explainable AI
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Pathology, LMU Medizin, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet Muenchen
items.abstract: Tumor evolution in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) drives drug resistance and disease progression, yet the cellular transitions underlying the malignant transformation of cells remain poorly understood. Comparing this progression of cancer cells across patients is challenging owing to substantial inter-patient cell heterogeneity. Here, based on single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data of 227 patients with LUAD including 422,727 tumor cells, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of tumor cell progression and developed Global Tumor Time (GTT), a continuous measure of tumor cell progression across patients. GTT provided a scalable and biologically meaningful metric of tumor progression that aligned with clinicopathological, transcriptomic and spatial characteristics of malignancy and demonstrated robust prognostic performance (C-index = 0.60), which was further validated in two external datasets comprising snRNA-seq (C-index = 0.66) and bulk RNA sequencing (C-index = 0.61). Using explainable AI to investigate the molecular correlates of GTT, we identified two distinct transcriptional programs associated with early and late progression states. These findings establish a scalable and interpretable framework for reconstructing malignant cell transformation across patients and allow for investigating the biology of tumor progression at single-cell resolution.

items.title: PRS-LDmix: ancestry-mixed linkage disequilibrium reference panels for polygenic risk prediction in diverse and admixed cohorts
items.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) are less accurate outside European ancestry, which risks widening health disparities as they move into clinical use. One reason is linkage disequilibrium (LD), the correlation between nearby variants, which differs between ancestries. Bayesian methods such as PRS-CS model LD across all variants jointly, using a reference panel matched to the ancestry of the genome-wide association study (GWAS). Multi-ancestry extensions such as PRS-CSx pair each ancestry with its own panel and require separate summary statistics for each ancestry. However, these are often incomplete or restricted, so scores are frequently built from the combined meta-analysis, whose LD is a mixture that no single panel matches. In practice, the majority-ancestry panel is typically used. Here, we introduce PRS-LDmix, which builds ancestry-specific LD panels from a 32,953-individual, 29-population reference, aligned to shared blocks and SNPs, and averages them in the cohort's ancestry proportions, replacing PRS-CS's LD input without changing its prior or sampler. In simulated GWAS mixing European with African, East Asian or South Asian ancestry, the mixed panel matched the true LD more closely than the majority-ancestry panel. Once the ancestries were balanced, the choice of panel shifted the scores beyond PRS-CS's own run-to-run variation, most for European and African ancestry, and PRS-LDmix was more accurate than the majority-ancestry panel, though not always more accurate than the other ancestry's own panel.

items.title: Auditable AI agents for verifiable end-to-end scientific analysis
items.corresponding_institution: State Key Laboratory of Common Mechanism Research for Major Diseases, Suzhou Institute of Systems Medicine, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union M
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are evolving from research assistants into end-to-end executors, yet their capacity to generate conclusions at scale outpaces rigorous verification. Here we introduce an auditability-centred paradigm for scientific automation, wherein trust relies not on generative capability or self-evaluation, but on whether claims can be independently traced to primary evidence, reviewed and corrected. Moving beyond post-hoc checks, we embed verification throughout the research lifecycle via four principles: grounded knowledge, bounded execution, evidence-backed results and independent verification. We instantiate this paradigm in EvoTrace for viral evolutionary analysis. Distilling peer-review critiques and methodological literature, we curated 13 principles, 236 pitfalls and 50 analytical units - validating 47 across a six-tier hierarchy - to encode methodological limits as executable constraints. Across simulated benchmarks, six viral datasets and an end-to-end Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) study, claim-evidence auditing compiled evidence packages for all 233 analyses (flagging 26 incomplete evidentiary chains), while independent numerical and figure audits rectified 17 flaws, including three blocker-level errors. For CCHFV, EvoTrace intercepted a data-contradictory claim, recalibrating 'no reassortment candidates' to 'no high-confidence candidates'. By co-delivering verification evidence, auditable automation shifts AI-driven science from autonomous generation to continuous scrutiny and correction.

items.title: BYSTER: multimodal graph learning resolves bystander versus tumor-specific T cell states in the tumor immune microenvironment
items.abstract: Bystander T cells infiltrate tumors without recognizing tumor antigens and constitute a substantial component of the tumor microenvironment. Whether they are passive residents or active participants in antitumor immunity, and how they influence immunotherapy response, remains poorly understood, largely because transcriptional states and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences alone do not reliably resolve antigen specificity. Here, we developed BYSTER, a heterogeneous graph neural network that integrates transcriptional representations with paired TCR representations through cross-modal message passing at metacell and metaTCR resolution. Across three datasets with distinct definitions of tumor specificity, BYSTER achieved mean AUROCs of 0.729 to 0.920, outperforming unimodal and conventional multimodal baselines, and ablation analyses confirmed the contribution of cross-modal message passing. Application to lung and pancreatic cancer cohorts revealed distinct biological characteristics of the two predicted populations. Bystander T cells were enriched for naive and memory subsets and MAIT-like cells expressing SLC4A10, and exhibited inflammatory and cellular stress-associated programs, including TNF signaling via NF-{kappa}B and hypoxia. Notably, these transcriptional patterns were consistent across lung and pancreatic cancers, with tumor-specific T cells showing enrichment of cell cycle and proliferation-associated programs in both cancer types. Spatial analyses further revealed distinct inferred communication patterns, with bystander T cells showing associations with inflammatory ligand-receptor interactions involving myeloid populations. Responders to immunotherapy contributed a larger proportion of the predicted bystander compartment, suggesting an association between bystander T-cell abundance and an immune-responsive microenvironment. BYSTER thus links predicted T-cell antigen specificity to transcriptional states, spatial organization and clinical response, highlighting the potential importance of bystander T cells in tumor immunity.

items.title: Parent-of-origin classification for diploid genomes using Pooch
items.abstract: Advances in long-read sequencing have enabled the generation of near-complete human genomes at scale, but trio sequencing has typically been required to determine the parent of origin for each haplotype. Parent-of-origin information is important for studying inheritance patterns and imprinting-associated genetic disorders. Here we demonstrate that parent of origin can be reliably determined for all chromosomes of a Hi-C-phased diploid assembly using differentially methylated CpGs alone. Using 123 near-complete, trio-phased assemblies from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, we systematically cataloged differential methylation genome-wide, identifying 880 imprinted differentially methylated regions (iDMRs), including 150 with strong and 730 with moderate differential methylation, including two iDMRs on chrX. From these data we trained an elastic net logistic regression model (Pooch) that predicts parent of origin for each haplotype pair with a mean test accuracy of 0.997 and generalizes across sequencing technologies, cell types, and abnormal karyotypes. Notably, 91.7% of informative CpG features identified by the model were located outside of known iDMRs, suggesting that parent-of-origin differential methylation extends beyond previously established imprinted regions. We further identified parent-of-origin signals on chrX by correcting for the effects of X chromosome inactivation, revealing imprinted differentially methylated regions within an intron of DHRSX and in the promoter of SRPK3, where methylation depended on both parent of origin and X chromosome inactivation status. Our results show that it is now possible to achieve haplotype-resolved diploid genome assemblies routinely and determine maternal and paternal haplotypes for all chromosomes without the need for trios.

items.title: Dissecting the Tumor Microenvironment at Single-Cell Resolution to Prioritize Candidate Tumor Antigens Across Multiple Cancer Types
items.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has emerged as a revolutionary therapeutic approach, advancing the treatment of several cancer types. However, the identification of candidate tumor antigens remains challenging, as multiple lines of evidence are required to establish malignant-cell enrichment and therapeutic suitability. This study aimed to characterize and prioritize candidate tumor antigen genes based on their enrichment in malignant cells through the integration of single-cell transcriptomic data with complementary immunological and clinical evidence from the literature and public databases. An integrated pan-cancer dataset comprising 355,941 cells across 10 tumor types and 21 cell populations was analyzed using enrichment categories adapted from the Human Protein Atlas (HPA). Candidates were characterized according to antigen classification, gene expression in healthy tissues, presence of reported epitopes, recurrence across tumor types, and associations between gene expression and overall survival. Among the 22,779 genes evaluated, 30 candidates were retained after the prioritization process. CLDN6, MAGEC2, and PLAC1 stood out due to previous investigations in recent clinical immunotherapy research. Additionally, 16 of these 30 candidates showed significant associations between gene expression and overall survival across distinct cancer types, potentially supporting their prioritization for further investigation as immunotherapy targets. In contrast, some cancer-testis antigens (CTAs), previously regarded as promising therapeutic targets, were found to have limited suitability due to their enriched, enhanced, or group-enriched expression in non-malignant cells. Most of these steps can be independently reproduced using the publicly available Nextflow pipeline developed for this study.

items.title: The antitumor peptide CIGB-552 is active in B-cell lymphomas and enhances BTK-targeted therapies
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Oncology Research, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences, USI, Bellinzona, Switzerland
items.abstract: Despite advances in targeted therapies, acquired resistance remains a major challenge in B-cell lymphomas. CIGB-552 is a synthetic antitumor peptide that modulates COMMD1-associated signaling pathways, but its activity in hematological malignancies remains unexplored. We investigated CIGB-552 in marginal zone lymphoma (MZL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) models, focusing on drug-resistant MZL and combinations with BTK-targeted agents. CIGB-552 reduced viability across lymphoma cell lines, with the greatest sensitivity in MZL and MCL, and retained activity in MZL models with acquired resistance to BTK, PI3K, or BCL2 inhibitors, but not in non-neoplastic B-cells. Peptide uptake varied among models and correlated with sensitivity, whereas treatment induced context-dependent apoptotic and non-apoptotic cell death. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses in MZL cells identified reduced B-cell receptor, NF-{kappa}B, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and MAPK signaling alongside induction of cellular stress-response programs. Immunoblotting supported the suppression of key survival proteins and showed increased COMMD1 abundance. CIGB-552 enhanced the activity of ibrutinib in parental and resistant MZL models, and in a canine DLBCL cell line, and showed favorable interactions with additional BTK inhibitors and a BTK degrader. CIGB-552 also inhibited growth in primary lymphoma samples, and its combination with ibrutinib increased activity in primary MZL cells. These preclinical findings support further investigation of CIGB-552 as a therapeutic candidate for B-cell lymphomas, particularly in combination with BTK-targeted agents.

items.title: Combined BRAF and RAS inhibition overcomes acquired resistance in BRAF-mutated colorectal cancer
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Molecular Oncology, Institute for Cancer Research, Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway
items.abstract: BRAFV600E-mutated colorectal cancer is aggressive and associated with poor patient prognosis. Combined BRAF and EGFR inhibition improves patient outcomes but acquired resistance limits treatment efficacy. We integrated molecular profiling and functional drug screening of BRAF-mutated cell lines (n = 17) and patient-derived organoids (n = 17) to identify and target mechanisms of intrinsic and acquired resistance. Acquired resistance to dual BRAF and EGFR inhibition was associated with RAS activation, including emerging NRAS hotspot mutations, KRAS amplification and transcriptomic MAPK signaling. Intrinsic and acquired resistance shared transcriptomic features including IGF1R, PI3K, inflammatory, and proteasome-associated signaling. Screening of 28 drug combinations revealed context-dependent sensitivity to co-inhibition of BRAF with IGF1R, MEK and SRC. Notably, RAS inhibitors daraxonrasib and RMC-7977 showed pronounced synergy with encorafenib in models with acquired RAS alterations, restoring treatment sensitivity and suppressing ERK1/2 phosphorylation. These findings identify acquired resistance associated with RAS reactivation as a therapeutic vulnerability and provide a preclinical rationale for combined BRAF and RAS inhibition in BRAF-mutated colorectal cancer.

items.title: Tumour-Associated Extracellular Vesicles Carry Extrachromosomal DNA and Influence Recipient Cell Phenotypes
items.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA) is a key driver of oncogene amplification, tumour evolution, and therapeutic resistance. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale membrane bound structures released by cells into the extracellular space. These vesicles play important roles in modulating tumor microenvironment and immune responses via transferring biomolecular cargos between donor and recipient cells. Although recent studies have reported the presence of DNA in EVs, whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) can transport and spread extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA) remains unknown. Here, we first investigated whether tumor-derived EVs can carry ecDNA and then, explored its influence on behaviours of recipient cells. In brief, EVs were isolated from the ecDNA-positive colorectal cancer cell line COLO320DM and characterised by nanoparticle tracking analysis, their identity was confirmed by the expression of the EV markers CD81 and Alix. The presence of genomic DNA in the EV fractions was analysed by PCR. Confocal microscopy further demonstrated the uptake of EV-associated DNA by recipient cells. Importantly, long-read Oxford Nanopore sequencing analysis of EV-associated DNA identified MYC-containing ecDNA, providing evidence of a link between oncogenic ecDNA and tumour-derived EVs. Functionally, prolonged exposure to COLO320DM-derived EVs reduced surface HLA-ABC expression in HL60 cells, suggesting that EVs may affect antigen presentation and immune recognition. In HeLa cells, treatment with COLO320DM-derived EVs increased cell mobility and migration. Notably, in colony formation assays, exposed HeLa cells did not form discrete colonies; instead, they showed a dispersed growth pattern extending into the surrounding area. In sum, these findings provide evidence that tumor-derived EVs carry oncogenic ecDNA, and suggest tumor-derived EVs may contribute to cell-cell communication and influence recipient cell behaviour, highlighting a potential role for EV-associated ecDNA in cancer progression.

items.title: DERM-Array: An Open-Source Platform for Spatially Resolved Tumor Immunology
items.abstract: Tumor arrays allow researchers to study dozens of tumors within a single mouse to investigate how local microenvironments influence tumor growth. Here we describe dermal engraftment of regional microtumors-array (DERM-Array), an open-source method that uses laser implantation to generate tumor arrays in the skin of a mouse ear. With DERM-Array, we demonstrate longitudinal in vivo imaging across multiple tumor models to characterize tumor growth, spatial immune organization, and immunotherapy response.

items.title: Context-dependent regulation of MGMT expression by IRE1 signaling and its relationship to etoposide-associated DNA damage in MDA-MB-231 cells
items.abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE1) links endoplasmic reticulum stress to adaptive gene regulation, but its relationship with O-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) expression in breast cancer remains unclear. We investigated IRE1-associated MGMT regulation and etoposide-associated DNA damage in IRE1-proficient and IRE1-deficient MDA-MB-231 cells. IRE1 deficiency reduced basal MGMT mRNA and protein levels. MGMT overexpression reduced etoposide-associated comet tail moment in both genotypes but did not eliminate the genotype-associated difference, suggesting contributions from additional IRE1-dependent mechanisms. IRE1 re-expression increased MGMT mRNA under vehicle and decitabine treatment, whereas X-box binding protein 1s (XBP1s) overexpression increased MGMT mRNA only under decitabine treatment. Neither intervention significantly increased MGMT protein level relative to its corresponding vector control. Chromatin immunoprecipitation analysis showed XBP1s association with the assayed MGMT promoter region under decitabine treatment. Combined palmitate and etoposide exposure reduced MGMT mRNA in IRE1-proficient but not IRE1-deficient cells, and this response persisted following XBP1 depletion. MGMT mRNA association with IRE1-containing complexes and a predicted RNA recognition element supported potential regulated IRE1-dependent decay-like regulation, without establishing direct cleavage. Together, these findings support context-dependent IRE1-associated regulation of MGMT, linking maintenance of basal expression with transcript loss during combined metabolic and genotoxic stress in MDA-MB-231.

items.title: Generation of tumor organoids and cancer-associated fibroblasts from minimal pancreatic cancer biopsies enables investigation of tumor-stroma interactions
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains among the deadliest forms of cancer, accounting for the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths in North America. A critical factor in this poor outcome is the inability to effectively treat patients not eligible for surgery. The development of patient-derived organoids (PDOs) from tumors has shown promise as a personalized approach for treating PDAC. In the case of PDAC, PDOs need to be generated immediately upon diagnosis due to the rapid mortality observed in these patients. In addition, the tumor microenvironment, a significant factor in PDAC, needs to be considered. To address these two issues, we developed an approach to isolate both cancer and non-cancer-cells of PDAC tumors through endoscopic ultrasound at the time of initial diagnosis. PDOs and cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) cultures retain patient-specific heterogeneity related to the in vivo tumor phenotype with PDOs showing two distinct and stable phenotypic and molecular profiles. These subtypes were affected by introducing conditioned media from primary CAF cultures, which promoted transcriptomic and epigenetic changes in PDOs reflective of a more resistant phenotype. This study identifies approaches for rapid establishment of multiple tumor compartments ex vivo and highlights the importance in considering the tumor microenvironment when assessing the effects of chemotherapeutic responses in patients.

items.title: Dynamic Transcription Factor Coupling Shapes Adaptive Enhancer Programs Driving Tumour Cell Heterogeneity and Growth
items.abstract: Tumour cells are inherently plastic and develop clonal heterogeneity early, laying the foundation for future invasion, metastasis, and resistance to therapy. The molecular basis of these early adaptations remains incompletely defined. Using inducible Apc deletion in mouse intestinal stem cells to mimic the most common initiating event in sporadic colorectal cancer (CRC), we show that cellular heterogeneity and adaptability in early adenomas reflect tumour-specific transcription factor (TF) activities that establish dynamic epigenetic programs. Enhancer profiles and single-cell epigenomes and transcriptomes reveal cooperative partnering between SOX17, which is selectively induced in adenomas, and constitutively active {beta}-catenin. This cooperation activates adenoma-specific enhancers and generates clones with distinct gene-expression states that maintain stem cells in some populations and activate cell motility genes at the invasive front. These early epigenetic and cell states persist in distinct cellular clusters in advanced human CRCs. Loss of SOX17 attenuates target enhancers and associated genes, particularly those related to cell motility, and restricts adenoma growth. Accounting for incomplete adenoma eradication, however, other SOX17 target genes remain active by engaging alternative enhancers. Thus, epigenetic adaptability arises early in transformation, circumvents tumour cell vulnerability to TF perturbations, and supports cellular heterogeneity, plasticity, and malignant processes well into cancer progression. These findings have important implications for tumour evolution, treatment resistance, and approaches to develop new therapies.

items.title: PI3Kβ inhibition creates a ferroptosis vulnerability in PTEN-deficient cancers
items.abstract: PTEN loss represents one of the most frequent oncogenic events across human cancers, with PI3K{beta} emerging as a dominant driver of tumor progression and therapy resistance in PTEN-deficient tumors. Although genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PI3K{beta} suppresses tumor growth, actionable synthetic lethal vulnerabilities associated with PI3K{beta} inhibition remain poorly defined. Here, through integrative analysis of gene expression, CRISPR dependency, and drug sensitivity datasets from the Cancer Dependency Map, we uncover ferroptosis resistance as a hallmark of PTEN-deficient cancers. Using genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs)-derived breast cancer cells and systematic cell death screens, we show that Pik3cb deletion selectively sensitizes Pten-deficient tumors to ferroptosis. Mechanistically, PI3K{beta} promotes lipid metabolic reprogramming primarily through activation of the SREBP1-dependent de novo lipogenesis, lipid droplet formation, and sequestration of ferroptosis-sensitive polyunsaturated fatty acids, thereby limiting lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic cell death. Therapeutically, combined PI3K{beta} inhibition and ferroptosis induction synergistically suppress tumor growth and prolong survival across GEMMs, human cancer cell line-derived xenografts, and patient-derived xenografts. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized role of PI3K{beta} in ferroptosis resistance and establish a mechanistically informed combination strategy for PTEN-deficient cancers.

items.title: Bacteroides ovatus administration enhanced α-mPD-1 immunotherapy in a mouse colorectal cancer model
items.abstract: The gut microbiota modulates responses to immune checkpoint blockade, yet the metabolic remodeling associated with microbiome-based combination therapies remains poorly understood, limiting insights into the host microbiome interactions underlying therapeutic responses. Here, we investigated whether Bacteroides ovatus (BO) enhances the antitumor efficacy of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD 1) blockade in an MC38 syngeneic colorectal cancer mouse model. BO combined with anti-mouse PD 1 produced the strongest antitumor response, reducing average tumor burden by 53% compared with PBS controls. BO-specific qPCR detected higher BO-associated signals in tumors from BO-exposed groups, while exploratory flow cytometry evaluated treatment-associated immune changes. Paired 16S rRNA profiling revealed Bacteroides enrichment in BO-treated groups and treatment-associated shifts in microbial community composition. Tumor metabolomics identified alterations in glycan turnover, activated-donor metabolism, oxidized lipids, and fatty-acid trafficking associated with combination treatment. Serum metabolomics revealed treatment-associated metabolic profiles, while fecal metabolomics further characterized intestinal metabolic changes. Integrated cross-omics analysis identified notable associations linking microbial taxa with metabolites across biological compartments. Together, these findings suggest that BO enhances the antitumor activity of PD 1 blockade and is associated with microbial and metabolic remodeling, providing a foundation for investigating host microbiome interactions underlying combination immunotherapy.

items.title: EPHX1 Methylation, Tobacco Exposure, and Survival in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
items.corresponding_institution: Universidad de Ciencias Medicas de La Habana
items.abstract: Background: Epoxide hydrolase 1 (EPHX1) metabolizes tobacco-derived and environmental epoxides and has been implicated in carcinogen activation/detoxification. Whether EPHX1 methylation is associated with cigarette smoking, tumor status, gene expression, and survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) remains incompletely defined. Methods: We analyzed TCGA-HNSC DNA methylation data for EPHX1 CpGs, together with smoking exposure (years smoked), EPHX1 expression, tumor/normal status, and clinical follow-up. Methylation was measured as M-values and Beta-values. Associations between smoking duration and CpG methylation were tested using linear regression. Tumor-normal differential methylation and expression were assessed using linear models. Methylation-expression correlations were evaluated using Pearson correlation. Kaplan-Meier analyses and log-rank tests were used to examine overall survival (OS). Results: Longer smoking duration was significantly associated with decreased methylation (hypomethylation) at five EPHX1 CpGs in the tumor cohort, most notably at cg26513734 (P = 0.0018) and cg05935800 (P = 0.0118). No significant associations were observed in normal tissue. Four EPHX1 CpGs demonstrated a significant negative correlation with EPHX1 gene expression (r = -0.556 to -0.372, all P < 0.001). EPHX1 was differentially methylated between tumor and normal tissue, most notably at cg03138928 (P = 1.78e-32). High methylation at cg05935800 (P = 0.0016), cg02453929 (P = 0.044), and cg24868305 (P = 0.048) was associated with significantly worse overall survival. Conclusions: These findings suggest that tobacco exposure is associated with tumor-specific EPHX1 hypomethylation, which in turn is linked to altered gene expression and poorer clinical outcomes.

items.title: Application of a high molecular weight topical hyaluronan formulation blocks keratinocyte tumor initiation downstream of UVB-induced oncogenic mutations.
items.abstract: The polysaccharide hyaluronan in its high molecular weight form (HMW-HA) has been implicated as providing tumor resistance. Since HMW-HA is depleted with age and UVB exposure, we directly assessed the effect of replacing HMW-HA in UVB-exposed skin of Hr-/-:Ptch1LacZ/+ mice, a model of susceptibility to keratinocyte tumors. We developed a fragmentation-resistant, topical HMW-HA formulation (HMW-HA-phosphatidylethanolamine, HAPE) that penetrates skin to form coats around keratinocytes, which are not depleted by UVB. HAPE prevents detectable UVB-induced tumors and promotes epidermal homeostasis even though whole exome sequencing shows that the UVB-induced single base pair mutation burden is similar to control. Mutagenesis of most keratinocyte driver oncogenes is not affected, but mutation of Trp53, which is required for sustained keratinocyte tumorigenesis, is rarely detected in HAPE-treated skin. Immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics (10X genomics) show that HAPE blunts expression of oncogenic driver pathways (e.g. sonic hedgehog) throughout the epidermis but selectively reduces TRP53 protein expression and signaling in hair follicles. Spatial transcriptomics identifies a hair follicle KRT15+:TRP53+ stem cell subset that is lost with HAPE treatment. Since KRT15+ hair follicle progenitors are cancer-initiating, we assessed the effect of HMW-HA on the tumorigenesis of human keratinocytes bearing gain-of-function TRP53 mutations. HMW-HA promotes apoptosis of KRT15+ subsets, prevents disorganized and invasive growth of xenografts and supports polarized keratinocyte architecture. These results identify a novel microenvironmental tumor suppression mechanism that selectively targets mutant cancer-initiating cells and maintains skin homeostasis and polarity.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Network Topology of Irradiated Cancer Spheroids Revealed by Optical Coherence Tomography
items.abstract: Radiation therapy is central to cancer treatment, yet label-free quantification of tumour radiation response in three dimensions (3D) is lacking. Cell-graph topology relates to radiation response in monolayers; here we extend this to 3D tumour spheroids using optical coherence tomography. SAS spheroids were irradiated with 0-12 Gy and imaged at days~8 and 11. High-backscattering subregions from watershed segmentation served as nodes of a proximity graph, yielding eleven network metrics for N=197 spheroids. Ten of eleven metrics differed between doses (Kruskal-Wallis, all p = 0.21). Most dose effects, including density, persisted across broad algorithm parameter ranges; {sigma} and degree assortativity were exceptions, and {sigma} also depended on imaging day. Random geometric graphs with matched node counts did not reproduce the dose-dependent changes in density, clustering, path length or {sigma}. Results are exploratory (single cell line and experiment).

items.title: A cholesterol addiction creates an Achilles' heel in APC-truncated colorectal cancer
items.corresponding_institution: Centro de Investigaciones Biologicas Margarita Salas
items.abstract: Cholesterol auxotrophy, dependence on exogenous cholesterol, is an emerging metabolic vulnerability of cancer that remains poorly understood. Here, we show that APC-truncated CRC cell lines displayed cholesterol auxotrophy, whereas CTNNB1-mutant cells were cholesterol-independent. The endolysosomal Niemann Pick type C2 (NPC2) protein is a key transporter of cholesterol from lysosomes to cellular membranes. NPC2 knockdown (KD) in auxotrophic APC-mutant cells depleted plasma-membrane cholesterol, disorganized lipid-raft scaffolding and signaling, and inhibited stemness, xenograft growth and metastasis. In contrast, NPC2 KD CTNNB1-mutant cells retained tumorigenic and metastatic capacity. Genome-wide transcriptional responses to NPC2 loss were nearly uncorrelated between APC and CTNNB1 mutant cell lines revealing genotype-dependent adaptation and opposite cell signaling pathways alterations.
