NPC2 KD auxotrophs showed abortive compensatory cholesterol synthesis with no alternative egress route, whereas CTNNB1-mutant cells restored lysosomal cholesterol egress by inducing NPC1 and sustaining Wnt/stemness identity, AP-1/YAP/TAZ signaling and a pro-invasive secretome. Lipidomics confirmed the signaling divergences: sphingomyelin collapse, membrane-fluidity remodeling exclusive to the auxotrophs, and opposite-direction diacylglycerol signaling in CTNNB1 mutants. Notably, APC-truncated cells phenocopied selected Niemann Pick type C hallmarks, linking lysosomal cholesterol export to tumor fitness. Thus, NPC2 constitutes a synthetic-lethal vulnerability specific to cholesterol-auxotrophic APC-mutant CRCs, providing a mechanistic rationale for targeting the secreted and recaptured NPC2 pool in this molecular subset of patients.

items.title: Discovery of novel drug combinations for oral squamous cell carcinoma through integrated analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets
items.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, yet treatment options remain limited and resistance driven by intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) is frequent. To characterize ITH and identify strategies to overcome it, we integrated twelve public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets into an unprecedentedly large dataset and combined it with spatial transcriptomics. A novel, pathway-based clustering approach revealed seven highly recurrent and distinct tumor cell clusters, each defined by divergent cell-cell interactions, distinct positions along the cell trajectory tree, and spatially defined localization within tumors. To overcome ITH therapeutically, we sought to identify drug targets that were overexpressed in the vast majority of these highly diverse tumor cells, which was reasonably achieved only through pairwise target combinations. Pharmacological inhibition of LGALS1 plus CTSC, and LGALS1 plus TYMP, suppressed growth of OSCC spheroids, with further enhancement by cisplatin. Additional anti-tumor activity is expected in vivo through known effects of these inhibitors on the tumor microenvironment. Our work characterizes ITH in OSCC and reveals strategies to overcome it by broadly targeting malignant and microenvironmental drivers of OSCC, providing a basis for the rational design of novel combination therapies.

items.title: Uncovering mechanisms of cell-free protein synthesis using tailored coarse-grained models
items.abstract: Cell-free protein synthesis has revolutionised molecular biology research, and it continues to be a fundamental methodology in synthetic biology today. Yet, many of its mechanistic principles remain poorly understood, limiting our ability to predict reaction behaviour. In this work, we introduce a pipeline for uncovering these principles that combines computational models with experimental validation in a design-build-test-learn cycle. First, we develop a coarse-grained ordinary differential equation model describing key processes in the reaction. Next, we adapt the model to predict system behaviour under competing mechanistic hypotheses and compare model predictions to our experimental data from batch reactions using Escherichia coli extract. Our data and analysis indicate that gene length determines the rate-limiting step in transcription; it identifies transcription/translation-independent depletion of chemical energy as the primary cause for reaction termination; and finally it highlights translation as the most variable process between batches of cellular extract. Together, these results point to strategies for improving the yield and reproducibility of cell-free protein synthesis, and provide a framework for rational, model-guided design of cell-free systems.

items.title: Engineering dynamic interkingdom communication between synthetic organelles and mammalian systems
items.abstract: Engineering intracellular microbes to function as synthetic organelles, or quasiorganelles, opens new avenues for controlling mammalian cell fates and function through programmable and quantitative interkingdom communication. Here, we develop a bioluminescent reporter platform to quantify the magnitude, kinetics, persistence, and spatial distribution of transcriptional regulation in mammalian host cells directed by quasiorganelles. Using an attenuated, flavin-auxotrophic Listeria monocytogenes chassis (LINQ1) engineered to deliver synthetic transcription factors, we demonstrate approximately 100-fold activation of mammalian reporter genes, with distinct kinetics and dynamics for the tetracycline transactivator and Gal4 systems. In transgenic reporter mice, LINQ1 induced approximately 25-fold reporter activation across multiple organs, with activity persisting beyond three weeks in some animals. In mice bearing triple-negative breast tumors, LINQ1 activated intratumoral transcription and, incidentally, transiently suppressed tumor growth, although responses diminished with repeated administration. These findings establish a quantitative foundation for engineering interkingdom communication in vivo to advance a new paradigm in which programmable microbial systems function as synthetic organelles to direct mammalian cell fates and function for therapeutic benefit.

items.title: Engineering acidophilic non-conventional yeasts as low-pH cell factories for organic acid production
items.abstract: Acidophilic non-conventional yeasts (NCYs) thrive at low pH and are promising hosts for organic acid production, but their use is limited by the availability of genetic engineering tools. Here, we optimised a chemical transformation protocol for efficient DNA delivery into six NCYs, including M. bulderi, S. bombicola, S. batistae, K. aerobia, K. naganishii and Y. lipolytica. We also developed Pan/ARS-containing expression vectors compatible with YeastFab for one-pot assembly of standardised promoters, open reading frames and terminators. As a proof of concept, we engineered M. bulderi, S. bombicola and S. batistae to produce lactic acid. We combined codon-optimised ldh genes from B. megaterium and L. helveticus with regulatory elements from S. cerevisiae or M. bulderi and introduced the resulting constructs into the hosts on episomal vectors. Lactic acid titres varied substantially across hosts and constructs. The highest titre, approximately 6.4 g/L, was achieved in S. batistae expressing the B. megaterium ldh gene under the control of S. cerevisiae regulatory elements. For targeted genome engineering, we developed a CREEPY-derived CRISPR-Cas9 system that supports multiplex gRNA assembly and achieved over 94% gene deletion efficiency in S. bombicola. In Starmerella species, Aro10p contributes to the conversion of pyruvate to acetaldehyde, potentially diverting carbon away from lactic acid production. Deleting ARO10 in S. bombicola increased lactic acid production through both endogenous and exogenous ldh pathways, with titres reaching up to 6 g/L. S. bombicola was unable to grow on lactate as the sole carbon source, whereas S. batistae utilised both D-lactate and L-lactate. This suggests that S. bombicola may offer a production advantage by limiting lactate reassimilation. Together, these genetic tools and metabolic engineering strategies expand the engineering capabilities of acidophilic NCYs and lay the groundwork for developing these yeasts as low-pH cell factories for the sustainable production of organic acids and other bio-based chemicals.

items.title: Natural and synthetic polyamines as organic counterions for multi-crossover DNA nanostructures
items.corresponding_institution: University at Albany, State University of New York
items.abstract: Assembly of DNA nanostructures requires positive counterions to shield the negative charge repulsion between the strands in the assembly. While several counterions have been explored for DNA nanostructure assembly, polyamines are particularly attractive candidates because they could support intracellular assembly of DNA nanostructures. However, a systematic analysis of natural and synthetic polyamines for DNA nanostructure assembly is currently lacking. In this study, we demonstrate the assembly of three model DNA nanostructures of the same size but with different number and topology of crossovers using three naturally occurring and two synthetic polyamines. The model DNA nanostructures are a double crossover motif with two antiparallel crossovers (DX-A), a double crossover motif with two parallel crossovers (DX-P), and a paranemic crossover with six parallel crossovers (PX). We successfully assembled all nanostructures, and relative assembly yields depended on the concentration and the type of polyamine and the type of DNA nanostructure. The structures exhibited comparable conformations but displayed slightly lower thermal stabilities compared to their Mg2+ assembled counterparts. We also demonstrate hierarchical assembly of DX tiles into periodic 2D lattices using the polyamines. Our results shed light on how polyamines differentially impact DNA nanostructures with distinct topological features and different crossover densities. Polyamines can serve as organic biocompatible counterions for the assembly of simple DNA motifs as well as larger arrays with implications for intracellular assembly and biological applications of DNA nanostructures.

items.title: Metabolism-Informed Bioreactor Model for Transferring Knowledge from Fed-batch to Continuous Biomanufacturing
items.corresponding_institution: The Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London, United Kingdom
items.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained high cell densities and volumetric productivities, but their operation depends on reliable real-time monitoring, prediction and control. Limited intracellular observability and sparse extracellular measurements hinder this, leaving a persistent gap between mechanistic understanding and predictive models used in practice. Here we describe a generalisable, metabolism-informed model that acts as a soft sensor for continuous bioprocess performance, enabling cross-regime deployment. The model uses measured concentrations as inputs and predicts intracellular fluxes. Mass balances at both the intracellular and reactor levels then constrain these fluxes and compute the extracellular metabolite concentrations at the next time point. Because these mass balances hold true across operating modes, they act as a fixed structural prior while the model's learned dynamics adapt to each regime. Our formulation does not use the predefined rate laws of standard kinetic models, nor does it assume steady state at the reactor level. We benchmark a genome-scale and a reduced metabolic network, and three optimisation strategies (max ATP, parsimonious FBA, flux sampling), and find that network size affects only flux interpretability, not concentration predictions, while optimisation strategy does not affect flux accuracy. After training on fed-batch data, we compare retraining strategies for continuous operation and find that retraining on limited continuous data works best. This agrees with our measured exchange fluxes, which vary mainly with growth rate rather than operating mode. These results point towards first-principles models that adapt to regime shifts.

items.title: A spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of the post-pneumonectomy lung
items.abstract: Perturbational spatial atlases have begun to map regenerative dynamics in a variety of tissues, yet lung remodeling has not been characterized at comparable spatial and temporal resolution. Post-pneumonectomy lung regeneration (PPLR) provides a tractable mammalian model for tissue regeneration that can be studied in situ. Here, we present a spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of PPLR in Rattus norvegicus, combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq), high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (10x Genomics Xenium), and NICHES-based spatial tissue connectomics. We observe three distinct tissue architectures at successive timepoints after pneumonectomy, each characterized by coordinated shifts in local cellular composition and intercellular signaling. At Day 3 (D3), a line of interstitial macrophages colocalizes directly beneath an intact mesothelium among active mechanotransductive and inflammatory signaling. We also observe the unexpected appearance of a transitional remodeling cellular community at D7 which appears largely absent at later timepoints, marked by fibrosis- mimetic signaling. At D14, an alveologenic architecture at distal lung tissue displays a connectivity signature consistent with active de novo growth, distinct from baseline homeostasis. Our findings establish a spatiotemporal map of multicellular architecture during regenerative lung remodeling and introduce a generalizable framework for spatial connectomic analysis to be used in perturbational tissue systems biology.

items.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals how the natural compound bostrycin induces iron starvation and ferroptosis
items.corresponding_institution: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany
items.abstract: The development of novel anticancer drugs remains urgent due to limited efficacy of existing therapies. Natural products are a rich source for discovery of anticancer agents, yet their mechanisms often remain elusive. Bostrycin, a fungal anthraquinone with broad cytotoxicity, is one such compound. Here, we combine global and nascent proteomics with metabolomics to elucidate the mechanism of bostrycin-induced cell death. We show that bostrycin induces ferroptosis, and use thermal proteome profiling to identify thioredoxin reductase 1 (TXNRD1), a key enzyme in glutathione metabolism and redox control, as bostrycin's primary direct target. Bostrycin triggered an iron starvation response and reduced iron-sulfur cluster-containing proteins, consistent with impaired cysteine availability. While the resulting iron overload likely triggered ferroptotic death, this coincided with broader disruption of redox balance, glutathione metabolism, and energy pathways. These findings establish bostrycin's mechanism of action and identify it as a ferroptosis-inducing agent acting distinctly from canonical inducers.

items.title: Tritrophic Interactions among Crapemyrtle, Crapemyrtle Aphids, and the Green Lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Burmeister)
items.abstract: Tritrophic interactions can have considerable impact on biological control systems, therefore, it is imperative to consider these interactions when implementing or evaluating biological control agents. Crape myrtles, Lagerstroemia indica L. x L. fauriei L., are important non-native ornamental plants from Asia that are widely planted and a major woody landscape species in the southern U.S. Six alkaloids have been identified from L. indica, mostly in the seeds and leaves. Crapemyrtle aphids, Tinocallis kahawaluokalani (Kirkaldy), are host specific to crape myrtle and have been shown to be important prey for many native beneficial insects including coccinellids, mirids, and green lacewings. The crapemyrtle aphids occur in different densities per leaf on crape myrtle cultivars and some native beneficial insects cannot fully develop by feeding solely on these aphids. Moreover, no parasitoids of crapemyrtle aphids are known. This information suggests that plant chemistry is involved in tritrophic interactions between this plant, its herbivores and their natural enemies. The purpose of this study was to investigate the suitability of crapemyrtle aphids as a food source for the green lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Bermeister). Experiments were conducted to test the effects of crapemyrtle cultivar, mature plant height, and source of germplasm on the life history characteristics of C. rufilabris. Crapemyrtle aphids were reared on seven cultivars of crapemyrtle, including Apalachee, Natchez, Sioux, Tuscarora, Lipan, Carolina Beauty, and Byers Wonderful White. Aphids from each cultivar were fed exclusively to green lacewing larvae from egg to adult eclosion. Survivorship by cultivar treatment was determined for developmental stages and growth parameters. Cultivar did not affect larval survival but did affect pupal and total survivorship. Length of pupation was extended by aphids feeding on mid mature height cultivars. Dry mass of larvae and adults were also affected accordingly. Males had lower dry mass than females. Lacewings fed on aphids from tall mature height cultivars developed higher dry mass.

items.title: A spatial transcriptomic map of subcutaneous adipose tissue aging in male mice
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Medicine, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE), Hamburg, Germany; Hamburg Center for Translational Immunology (HCTI) and Center for B
items.abstract: Aging alters adipose tissue composition and function, but the spatial organization and gene expression dynamics during lifetime remain incompletely characterized. Here we profiled spatial transcriptome-wide changes in the aging male murine inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT). We describe ten different cell type clusters and three distinct adipocyte states. Further, we detected lipid-associated macrophages (LAMs), the cell type-enriched cluster with the largest number of genes upregulated in old age. LAMs that engage in local crown-like structures (CLS) are associated with pro-inflammatory niche programs at old age while LAMs outside of CLS are enriched in metabolically active transcriptional programmes at young age. LAM spots show reduced predicted lipid oxidation and glycolytic activity with age. Independent validation confirmed functionally reduced glycolytic capacity in aged female and male LAMs. Together, our study provides a deeply sequenced spatiotemporal resource for investigating adipose tissue aging biology, and for prioritizing spatially defined macrophage niches.

items.title: Subsequent Phases of Gene Expression Leading to Commitment and Differentiation in a Eukaryotic Cell
items.abstract: Cell differentiation requires the specific control of gene expression for each cell type. However, the mechanism by which robust developmental outcomes arise from inherently noisy single-cell dynamics remains unclear. To address this question, we performed a formal analysis of longitudinal time series during the commitment and differentiation of giant single cells. We tracked how the discrete expression states of individual genes changed relative to each other. Despite marked variability in timing and trajectories from cell to cell, we identified reproducible temporal motifs and quantified the strength of temporal correlations among early- and late-regulated genes. Notably, a core gene set exhibited the same relative temporal order in establishing stable or transiently stable expression states in most cells. This suggests that a well-defined gene expression program emerges amidst apparent stochasticity. These results support a model in which induction to differentiation proceeds via a cascade of partially concurrent, discrete genetic switching events that collectively produce gradual, continuous shifts in expression at the population level. This framework reconciles apparently stochastic single-cell behavior with reliable developmental outcomes and suggests general principles for the temporal organization of gene regulation during differentiation. Furthermore, it provides analytic tools that can be broadly applied to longitudinal single-cell datasets to design temporally precise interventions in development and disease.

items.title: Spectral analysis of gene-dependency networks reveals emergent organization across scales in CAR T biology
items.abstract: CAR T-cell infusion products are commonly characterized in terms of their cellular populations and transcriptional programs, but these descriptions do not fully capture how a product is organized as a system. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from the infusion products of 163 patients across eight cohorts to investigate how system-level transcriptional organization relates to both clinical outcome and how cellular features vary together across patients. For each patient, we constructed a gene-dependency graph using mutual information between the binary detection states of each gene pair across infusion cells. To characterize each patient's network architecture, we define spectral organization, O{lambda}, a measure of the relative persistence of collective patterns of gene dependence in the network. Using hierarchical Bayesian survival models, we assessed the associations of both O{lambda} and various established cellular features with treatment outcome. Higher spectral organization was associated with a higher hazard of treatment failure in both a continuous model (hazard ratio per standard deviation, 1.45, 95% credible interval 1.07-2.19) and a smooth transition model (hazard ratio comparing the high and low regimes, 2.03, 95% credible interval 1.10-3.53). When we investigated how cellular features covary across patients, we found that correlations among both T-cell programs and cell type proportions aligned more coherently with treatment failure risk in the high O{lambda} regime compared to the low regime, revealing a systems-level pattern that helps explain the clinical relevance of spectral organization. Gene set enrichment analysis further showed that more persistent architectures were associated with inflammation and cellular interaction pathways, whereas lower spectral organization was associated with biosynthetic and genome maintenance pathways, consistent with the hypothesis that the organizational state of an infusion product reflects its capacity to reconfigure in response to CAR T treatment. Altogether, our findings identify spectral organization as a property of the infusion product as a whole that connects gene-dependency architecture within individual products to the collective variation of cellular features across patients. This framework therefore motivates studying CAR T biology from a systems perspective alongside established descriptions of cellular state.

items.title: Representational geometry shapes noise-driven working memory errors
items.abstract: Humans and other animals have strictly limited working memory capacity. When asked to recall one or more presented items after a delay period, subjects will occasionally recall an apparently random item: a "guess'' response. Where do these guesses come from? Using electrophysiological recordings from across monkey neocortex during the performance of a color working memory task, we show that the neural correlates of guess responses emerge during the memory delay -- and that variable encoding precision makes guesses more likely, especially in one of our two animals. If guess responses emerge due to noise, we hypothesize that the detailed neural population geometry for color should shape the distribution of behavioral responses. We confirm this hypothesis by showing that the representational geometry specific to each animal is consistent with their idiosyncratic patterns of errors. Despite the often assumed robustness of neural population representations, noise appears to be a key bottleneck on the reliability of working memory.

items.title: Information Content of Cortical Recordings During Deep Brain Stimulation in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
items.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate network brain activity across both cortical and deep brain (ventral-capsule/ventral-striatum; VC/VS) sites in patients with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) that were receiving DBS treatment. We sought to identify relationships between activity in both brain sites, and interactions between them, with evolution of OCD symptomology over treatment. We hypothesized that recordings from cortical sites would carry unique informational content that could predict symptoms and support future adaptive stimulation designs. Materials and Methods: Two patients with severe treatment refractory OCD were implanted with electrodes targeting VC/VS and the supplementary motor area (SMA) bilaterally. Electrodes were connected to Medtronic implantable pulse generators (PC+S or Percept) and could both deliver stimulation and record ongoing local field potential activity. Patients underwent approximately two years of stimulation treatment during which clinical measures of OCD symptoms and brain recordings were regularly collected. Results: Spectral features of VCVS and SMA brain activity had significantly higher entropy (information content) in the signal recorded from the cortical site. A mass univariate partial correlation analysis, controlling for confounders, revealed that cortical and VCVS-cortical interactions were highly represented among the features significantly associated with symptom evolution over the course of treatment (Patient 1: 20 of 30 significant features; Patient 2: 22 of 30 significant features; permutation based false discovery rate correction at q < 0.05). Conclusions: Our findings underscore the importance of capturing cortical activity and VCVS-cortical interactions during DBS research for OCD, with potential implications for the development of more informed and personalized stimulation strategies, including adaptive DBS.

items.title: Shank3 loss heightens social engagement among sibling cagemates and antagonism toward strangers
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with strong genetic contributions and diverse social impairments. However, it remains unclear how autism-linked mutations alter social behavior across social contexts and relationships. Using SLEAP multi-animal pose tracking, we followed complete Shank3 knockout (exon 4-22 deletion) mice with adult male and female sibling cagemates over four weeks and with strangers. Unexpectedly, knockouts initiated more social contact and allogrooming with familiar cagemates. Individual differences in social behavior and preferences for specific cagemates remained stable over time across genotypes. With strangers, knockout mice showed less nose-to-nose contact, more nose-to-base contact, and more chasing. Unlike wild-type mice, knockouts did not increase contact with strangers relative to siblings. These genotype differences were not detected in conventional three-chamber sociability and social novelty assays. These findings reveal that Shank3 loss reshapes social behavior in context-specific ways, enhancing engagement with familiar partners while altering threat responses to social novelty.

items.title: Nanobody-guided proximity proteomics reveals conformationally encoded molecular neighborhoods of LRRK2
items.abstract: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is a multidomain signaling protein implicated in Parkinson's disease whose activity is closely linked to conformational state. How these structural transitions shape the cellular molecular environment of LRRK2 remains poorly understood. Here, we combined nanobody-mediated conformational control with miniTurbo proximity proteomics to define molecular neighborhoods associated with inhibitory, neutral, and activating LRRK2 states. Structural modeling suggested that the activating nanobody Nb22 targets the WD40 domain and destabilizes interactions maintaining the autoinhibited conformation. Consistent with this model, activation was accompanied by ordered, reciprocal remodeling of the LRRK2 proximity proteome, with progressive enrichment of centrosomal, ciliary, and RAB/endolysosomal machinery and depletion of soluble cytosolic, proteostasis-associated and 14-3-3 proteins. Notably, the Nb22-associated proteome combined centrosomal and endolysosomal components previously linked to distinct LRRK2 signaling environments. These findings support a model in which conformational transitions reorganize the spatial molecular neighborhood of LRRK2 and thereby couple kinase state to distinct cellular signaling networks.

items.title: Multimodal dynamics during naturalistic learning are associated with subsequent performance
items.abstract: Learning from continuous material involves dynamic coordination of visual sampling, autonomic arousal, and neural activity, yet how these signals jointly organize during successful learning remains unclear. Here, we analysed synchronized eye-tracking, pupillometry, and EEG recordings from 86 participants from the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset. Using hidden Markov modelling, we identified recurrent multimodal states after accounting for stable recording-level differences and stimulus-shared responses. Three reproducible states with distinct psychophysiological profiles emerged. Poorer subsequent quiz performance was associated with greater relative expression of a state characterized by longer fixations, reduced fixation and saccade rates, lower gaze entropy, elevated pupil level and variability, and distinct EEG spectral entropy and frontoparietal theta coherence. In contrast, better performance was associated with greater expression of a state characterized primarily by more frequent and larger phasic pupil dilations. Quiz performance was also positively associated with transitions from this phasic-pupil state to the dominant background state, whereas relative expression of the dominant state itself showed no robust association with performance. The transition association did not survive correction in common-record window-length sensitivity analyses. These findings indicate that learning during naturalistic viewing is associated with the dynamic coordination of multiple ocular, pupillary, and neural signals, with relative state balance and directed transition probabilities each associated with subsequent quiz performance.

items.title: Gentle touch modulates late spinal and cortical somatosensory responses without detectable changes in spinal component N13 and nociceptive flexion reflex amplitude
items.corresponding_institution: Instituto de Psicoloxia (IPsiUS), Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Santiago de Compostela, Spain
items.abstract: Affective and gentle touch have been associated with changes in pain and somatosensory perception, but it remains unclear whether these effects reflect early spinal gating or later cortical and descending processes. We investigated whether gentle touch with CT-optimal characteristics modulates spinal and cortical somatosensory and nociceptive processing across three experiments. Experiment 1 compared the sural-nerve nociceptive flexion reflex (NFR; RIII) in the leg while the forearm received no touch, vibration, robot-delivered brushing, or human-delivered stroking. Experiment 2 compared somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs) across the same four conditions. Experiment 3 compared robot-delivered brushing with no touch, including additional trials to improve sensitivity to spinal SEP modulations. RIII amplitudes and spinal (N13, P22) and cortical (N20, P25, N30, P45, N60, P150) SEP components were analyzed. Gentle touch modulated neither the heterosegmental NFR nor the segmental N13, arguing against inhibition of early afferent transmission within or beyond the touched segment. However, Experiment 3 revealed modulation of the P22 spinal component, suggesting that gentle touch may influence spinal processing through supraspinal feedback mechanisms. At the cortical level, both robot- and human-delivered gentle touch attenuated the N60 and P150 components relative to vibration and no-touch conditions, indicating modulation of later stages of somatosensory processing consistent with attentional and cognitive influences. These findings suggest that CT-optimal gentle touch does not act through direct segmental inhibition of incoming sensory signals, but instead modulates later spinal and cortical processing, likely through descending influences. This study provides a multilevel neurophysiological framework for understanding how affective touch shapes sensory processing.

items.title: Longitudinal Increases in Ventral Attention Network Connectivity Predict Heightened Reward and Punishment Sensitivities via Self-Control Decline in Emerging Adulthood
items.abstract: Emerging adulthood is a critical developmental window for the maturation of executive control and the reorganization of intrinsic brain networks. However, the longitudinal neurobiological mechanisms underlying changes in cognitive control?and their associations with trait sensitivities?remain poorly understood. In a two-year longitudinal study, 332 emerging adults underwent behavioral assessments and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Latent Change Score Modeling (LCSM) revealed that longitudinal increases in reward and punishment sensitivities were primarily predicted by the progressive decline in self-control, rather than baseline or concurrent impulsivity. Neurally, by targeting the macroscopic connectome utilizing rigorous change score models adjusted for baseline variances and longitudinal head motion, we found that longitudinal increases in intra-network connectivity within the Ventral Attention Network (VAN) specifically and robustly tracked this self-control decline. Furthermore, a unified path analysis revealed a robust full mediation mechanism: heightened VAN intra-network connectivity predicted increased environmental sensitivities strictly through the decline in self-control. These findings identify increased VAN connectivity as a specific neural marker of diminished cognitive control, highlighting the preservation of self-control capacity as a key mechanistic target for promoting adaptive resilience during emerging adulthood.

items.title: Developmental timing of gene expression predicts dosage dominance, which tracks neuronal-glial fate in the developing human brain
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Integrated Biomedical and Life Science, Korea University, Seoul, 02841, Republic of Korea; L-HOPE Program for Community-Based Total Learning Healt
items.abstract: Genes implicated in brain disorders have diverse functions, but how altered dosage shapes their effects on developmental cell fate remains unclear. In a cell-state dynamics model of the developing human brain, genes expressed earlier in development responded more strongly to knockout than to overexpression, and this dosage dominance tracked neuronal-glial fate. Fate responses of 14,044 genes formed 31 modules across 21 lineages. Stronger perturbations could reverse fate responses despite correlated predicted expression changes across neuronal destinations. Disease-risk genes occupied shared and distinct developmental programs. Within autism, module timing distinguished genes associated with and without intellectual disability or developmental delay, while de novo and common variation implicated different modules. Knockout signatures of selected autism-associated modules matched the neuronal-down, glial-up pattern that postmortem autism cortex shares with other psychiatric disorders. These findings connect heterogeneous genetic risk through developmental programs whose fate responses depend on dosage and cellular context.

items.title: Altered ultrasonic vocalizations in mouse models of FOXG1 syndrome
items.abstract: FOXG1 syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with communication impairment as a defining clinical feature, yet vocal behavior has not been characterized in animal models of FOXG1. We examined neonatal ultrasonic vocalizations in two mouse models that disrupt Foxg1 in distinct developmental and cellular contexts: a NEX-Cre-driven conditional heterozygous model targeting postmitotic cortical and hippocampal excitatory neurons, and a W300X/+ knock-in model carrying a patient derived truncating mutation at the endogenous Foxg1 locus. Vocalizations were recorded at postnatal day 7 and analyzed for call number, duration, frequency range, and repertoire composition. The two models exhibited distinct vocal phenotypes. Conditional heterozygous mice produced longer calls while total vocal output, frequency range, and repertoire composition were preserved. In contrast, W300X/+ mice produced shorter calls, showed a significant shift in repertoire composition, and a non-significant trend toward reduced vocal output. The effect of genotype on call duration differed significantly between models, demonstrating opposing effects on temporal vocal structure. Frequency range was not significantly altered by genotype in either model, although sex was associated with frequency range in the conditional heterozygous cohort. These findings provide the first evidence that Foxg1 disruption alters neonatal vocal behavior and show that the resulting phenotype depends on the developmental, cellular, and molecular context of the mutation. Neonatal vocalizations therefore provide a sensitive behavioral readout for distinguishing functional consequences of disease relevant FOXG1 perturbations.

items.title: Automated neuroimaging meta-analysis through LLM-guided selection improves recovery of published spatial patterns
items.abstract: Systematic meta-analysis enables cumulative science, but expert-led, manual workflows do not scale with the growing literature. In neuroimaging, automated frameworks are widely used but typically sacrifice precision by using coarse article selection and pooling reported results, combining different tasks, populations or comparisons even when only a subset is relevant. Here we present AutoNIMA, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that screens articles using expert-defined eligibility criteria and parses heterogeneous tables to extract brain stereotactic coordinates and select relevant analyses within each article. AutoNIMA produced maps more closely matching expert-curated references than a search-only baseline representing existing automated methods in 26 of 27 meta-analyses. Analysis-level selection accounted for most of the improvement. These findings demonstrate how LLM-guided curation can filter relevant analyses within the same paper and support scalable neuroimaging evidence synthesis.

items.title: Loss of TTC5 impairs cortical development, disrupts tubulin homeostasis and progenitor mitosis in vivo
items.corresponding_institution: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania
items.abstract: Objective Loss-of-function mutations in the multifunctional scaffolding protein tetratricopeptide repeat domain 5 (TTC5) cause Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Cerebral Atrophy and variable Facial Dysmorphism (NEDCAFD), a recently described neurogenetic syndrome. TTC5 autoregulates tubulin translation in vitro; however, the role of TTC5 in brain development in vivo is poorly understood. Here, we define the function of TTC5 in neocortical development. Methods We established a mouse model carrying a recurrent patient nonsense mutation (TTC5R263*/R263*) causing NEDCAFD, and investigated cortical progenitor development, tubulin homeostasis, microtubule function, and neuronal morphogenesis using in vivo, in vitro, and transcriptomic approaches. Results The TTC5R263* mutation was a strong loss-of-function allele, with homozygous newborns exhibiting neonatal lethality, reduced brain size, and loss of cortical neurons. These developmental abnormalities arise from an early and persistent loss of neural progenitor expansion and impaired neuronal differentiation during corticogenesis, associated with defective mitotic progression, altered cell fate determination, and increased DNA damage. We further investigate TTC5 as a regulator of tubulin homeostasis during cortical development in vivo. Loss of TTC5 reduced tubulin mRNA and protein levels. Furthermore, TTC5R263*/R263* primary neurons exhibit reduced microtubule growth dynamics and defective neuronal arborization. Transcriptomic analyses of TTC5R263*/R263* developing cortex identify differentially expressed genes and pathways involved in neurodevelopmental processes, including coordinated dysregulation of cell-cycle regulators and a multitude of microtubule-associated gene pathways. Interpretation TTC5 is essential for cortical progenitor expansion, mitotic progression, and tubulin homeostasis during cortical development. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for NEDCAFD pathogenesis in vivo.

items.title: Learning human robot collaboration reshapes biological motor coordination
items.corresponding_institution: MRC Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit, University of Cambridge
items.abstract: Wearable augmentation robots expand human motor capabilities, but every added degree of freedom creates a new coordination problem for the biological body. Although previous studies have made substantial advances in robot sensing, control, and safety, they have largely overlooked how the users own movement changes: individuals adapt their body movements when they start using an augmentation robot, even when control does not require it, and this coordination pattern continues to change as they gain proficiency. Consequently, users may struggle to accommodate robot-related restructuring of their movements during prolonged use, potentially increasing the risk of user rejection or abandonment. Over five days of training, 26 participants performed tasks with a wearable robotic digit and a tool-use control task, allowing us to longitudinally characterise and compare body-wide movement patterns between the two. Performance improved similarly across tasks, but the underlying motor coordination trajectories diverged. During augmentation, biological finger and limb coordination departed progressively further from its initial structure than during tool use, and joints increasingly varied together in ways that kept task performance stable, indicating that a new, body-wide augmented motor pattern continued to develop across days. These findings demonstrate that the biological motor system is not a fixed substrate that can be simply augmented with artificial limbs, but rather its movement patterns continuously evolve as users learn to control an added effector. Characterising this evolving motor solution informs the design, training, and evaluation of augmentation systems, supporting the sustained integration of added effectors into the human motor system.

items.title: Auditory cortical population codes for pitch are cue dependent
items.abstract: Pitch provides a powerful example of perceptual invariance, enabling us to recognize the same melody across different instruments. The fundamental frequency (F0) at which a pitch is heard can be derived from either the harmonic spacing of frequency components (spectral cues), the waveform periodicity (temporal cues), or both. It is unclear whether population codes for F0 in auditory cortex are invariant across these acoustic cue classes. We addressed this question by training a linear decoder to predict F0 from the spiking responses of 1085 neurons in ferret primary auditory cortex to 10 sound types varying in their spectral and temporal composition. F0 could be decoded accurately when trained and tested on any individual sound type. However, decoding performance generalised well across sounds only if they contained the same class of pitch cue, and poorly between complex sounds and pure tones. Onset and offset responses carried different information about the F0 of complex sounds. Finally, approximately 20 neurons were sufficient to decode F0, but F0 information was widely distributed across the neural population. These findings show that F0 is represented in primary auditory cortex in cue-dependent, temporally multiplexed subspaces, with sparse pitch representations embedded in a distributed, robust population code.

items.title: β-Adrenergic regulation of mGluR5-dependent Ca2+ signalling in reactive astrocytes
items.corresponding_institution: LN-MCP, Institute of Pathophysiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Ljubljana
items.abstract: Astrocytes support neuronal function and brain homeostasis and undergo structural and functional remodelling under pathological conditions. Here, we compared astrocytes maintained in serum-containing medium, modelling a blood-brain barrier-compromised reactive state, with serum-free conditions that promote a more physiological arborised phenotype. We examined surface expression and signalling of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), {beta}-adrenergic receptors ({beta}-ARs), and pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide type 1 receptor (PAC1) as well as expression of excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2). Live-cell immunolabelling combined with optophysiological measurements revealed that serum-exposed reactive astrocytes had substantially reduced surface mGluR5 expression and negligible mGluR5-dependent Ca2+ signalling, accompanied by increased expression of EAAT2. Adrenergic stimulation and sustained cAMP elevation restored surface mGluR5 expression and (S)-3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine (DHPG)-evoked Ca2+ responses while reducing EAAT2 expression despite continued serum exposure. Reactive astrocytes also showed enhanced, prolonged {beta}-AR-mediated cAMP responses that were largely uncoupled from changes in intracellular Ca2+. These findings demonstrate coordinated remodelling of glutamatergic and {beta}-adrenergic signalling in reactive astrocytes. The capacity to restore mGluR5-dependent signalling is retained and strongly regulated by cAMP, suggesting that neuromodulatory pathways can modulate astrocytic glutamate responsiveness independently of a complete reversal of the reactive phenotype.

items.title: The Developing Human Connectome Project: Fetal Data Release
items.corresponding_institution: Centre for the Developing Brain, School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences, King's College London, London UK.; Research Department of Early Life Ima
items.abstract: The Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) represents a large open science resource designed to enable detailed investigations of typical and atypical brain development across the perinatal period. It consists of 1228 multimodal magnetic resonance image examinations of the fetal and/or neonatal brain from 1173 participants, together with collateral demographic, clinical, family, neurocognitive and genomic data. All subjects were studied in utero and/or soon after birth with a single MRI scanner using specially developed scanning sequences with novel motion-tolerant imaging methods and optimised for the changing properties of the developing brain. The neonatal data has been described and released separately. The fetal data release consists of multimodal data from 273 subjects scanned between 20 + 6 and 38+2 weeks (+days) of gestation, with some fetuses imaged more than once to provide longitudinal data creating 297 datasets in total. The data include: high resolution and motion corrected T1 and T2 weighted anatomical images; high temporal resolution functional and multi-shell high angular resolution diffusion MRI; and multimodal age-resolved atlases; together with demographic, family and clinical data, genomic and epigenomic data and follow-up neurodevelopmental assessment at around 18 months. This paper describes the dHCP fetal image acquisition, reconstruction and processing protocols, summarizes the available data, and provides information on how it can be accessed.

items.title: The metacognitive signatures of imposterism
items.abstract: The imposter phenomenon (or imposterism) is a commonly reported psychological pattern in which individuals persistently doubt their abilities and accomplishments despite objective evidence of their competence. Imposterism is associated with chronic self-doubt and reduced well-being, yet its cognitive mechanisms remain unclear. In a large online sample (N = 602), we investigated how self-reported imposter feelings relate to decision-making, confidence and information search in a perceptual decision-making task. Imposterism was associated with lower confidence in perceptual decisions and increased information seeking, despite not being associated with any detriment in objective perceptual performance. Though symptoms of anxiety and depression contributed to the relationship between imposterism and confidence, imposterism uniquely predicted increased information-seeking. Interestingly, the increased information seeking associated with imposterism did not lead to an imposterism-specific increase in final decision performance and did not alleviate overall uncertainty: imposterism remained associated with reduced confidence even for final decisions. To explain this, we hypothesised that information seeking may compensate for maladaptive second-guessing. Supporting this, imposterism predicted greater response switching and decreases in accuracy on trials where no additional information was sought, reflecting counterproductive changes of mind. These effects were absent on trials where information was accessed, suggesting that seeking additional information helped buffer against maladaptive second-guessing. Overall, our findings show that imposterism is marked by low confidence, heightened information seeking, and vulnerability to second-guessing in the absence of external reassurance. These results provide novel insights into distortions of self-evaluation in imposterism and highlight a compensatory role for information seeking in stabilising performance. Our study advances understanding of a widely discussed yet underexplored psychological phenomenon with significant implications for education, workplace wellbeing, and mental health.

items.title: Fibronectin binding and non-canonical transcription factor signature distinguishes lung and bone marrow megakaryocytes
items.corresponding_institution: University of Utah, Molecular Medicine Program
items.abstract: Recent evidence has demonstrated the unique morphology and function of lung megakaryocytes (MKs), yet the source of the differences between lung and bone marrow (BM) MKs remains unclear. While BM MKs are large, polyploid, BM-resident cells primarily known as platelet producing cells, lung MKs are smaller, less polyploid, and known for immunomodulation. To better understand the factors underlying the differences in lung and BM MKs, we developed a flow cytometry method for precise characterization and isolation of MKs using leukocyte exclusion and examination of hematopoietic and canonical MK markers. When MK-leukocyte aggregates are excluded, a single femur+tibia contains approximately 1,493 MKs and a single lung contains approximately 4,541 MKs. Enrichment via positive selection efficiently removes unwanted cells, increasing the percentage of MKs amongst live lung cells by 10.29-fold and the percentage of MKs amongst live BM cells by 29.09-fold. Sorted MKs were viable and spread onto fibrinogen. Gene expression analysis demonstrated that lung MKs increase immune pathway gene expression, including TNFRSF1B. Transcription factor (TF) and cell cycle gene expression decreased in lung MKs compared to BM MKs, including reduced expression of GATA1 and CDC6, possibly explaining observations of low ploidy and size in lung MKs, while expression of the TF ETS2 increased. Lung MKs also express increased ITGA4 compared to BM MKs, abundant surface integrin 4 protein, and increased surface integrin {beta}7 protein compared to BM MKs. Additionally, lung MKs bind significantly more fibronectin ex vivo then BM MKs. These data demonstrate for the first time that lung MKs have a unique TF signature and suggests integrin 4{beta}7 as a relevant receptor for lung MK function.

items.title: Nsg2 deficiency attenuates intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated tumorigenesis through microbiome-dependent metabolic remodeling
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Internal Medicine and Liver Research Institute, Seoul National University College of Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea
items.abstract: Background & Aims Neuron-Specific Gene 2 (NSG2) is a neuronally expressed protein that facilitates excitatory synaptic transmission through the regulation of AMPA receptor trafficking. While its function has been characterized in the central nervous system, whether NSG2 plays a role in enteric neuronal signaling and intestinal pathology has yet to be explored. We therefore investigated whether Nsg2 deficiency modulates intestinal inflammation and tumorigenesis through gut microbiome-dependent mechanisms. Methods Dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and azoxymethane/DSS-induced colitis-associated cancer (DSS-CAC) models were established in Nsg2-/- and wild-type (WT) mice. Disease severity was evaluated using the disease activity index (DAI), histopathological scoring, and tumor burden assessment. To investigate the potential contribution of the gut microbiota to genotype-associated phenotypes, WT and Nsg2-/- mice were co-housed for six weeks before disease induction. Gut microbial composition and predicted functional pathways were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region) and PICRUSt2, respectively. Results Separately housed Nsg2-/- mice exhibited significantly attenuated DSS-induced colitis, with reduced body weight loss, lower DAI scores, and preserved colonic architecture. In the DSS-CAC model, Nsg2-/- mice developed significantly fewer and smaller tumors with suppressed Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Under co-housing conditions, no statistically significant differences in colitis severity or tumor burden were detected between genotypes, supporting a possible contribution of the gut microbiota to the phenotypes observed in separately housed mice. 16S rRNA sequencing identified distinct microbial communities in Nsg2-/- mice, characterized by greater alpha diversity and enrichment of protective taxa, including Butyricicoccus and Lachnospiraceae. Functional profiling predicted enrichment of methane metabolism, porphyrin biosynthesis, and one-carbon metabolism pathways. Conclusions Nsg2 deficiency confers protection against intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated tumorigenesis, accompanied by alterations in gut microbial composition and suppression of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. These findings identify NSG2 as a novel modulator at the intersection of enteric neuronal signaling, gut microbiota, and mucosal immunity, positioning it as a potential therapeutic target for IBD and inflammation-driven colorectal cancer.

items.title: Single cell mapping reveals phenotypic, immunometabolic and functional heterogeneity among age-associated B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and aging
items.abstract: Abstract/Summary Introduction: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) comprise an antigen-experienced memory B-cell population that expands during aging but has also been implicated in autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Cell immunometabolism has emerged as a key determinant of immune-cell function, linking metabolic adaptation to both protective and maladaptive immunity or pathological inflammation, thereby providing a platform for therapeutic intervention. This study aims to comprehensively profile the functional alterations that accommodate ABC expansion, emphasizing metabolic reprogramming within the B-cell compartment in SLE, particularly with regard to ABCs, in order to identify niche metabolic pathways utilized by ABCs that may represent useful therapeutic targets. Methods: An exploratory analysis was conducted using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to phenotypically and functionally characterize ABC populations in patients with SLE and lupus-prone MRL.lpr mice, using a broad array of community tools. We further conducted SCENITH-based metabolic profiling to assess metabolic differences among splenic follicular (FO), marginal zone (MZ) and CD21-CD23- double negative (DN) B cells, in the murine SLE-like MRL.lpr model, in which we tested the ability of B cell subsets to generate protein output, following exposure to specific metabolic inhibitors (2-deoxyglucose and oligomycin). In addition, we cross-examined CD21-CD23- DN B cells in the native context of aging by employing flow cytometry-based analyses of their redox status (NADH/FAD autofluorescence) and mitochondrial function (MitoTracker and TMRE staining) to investigate age-associated metabolic programming. Results: Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed substantial immunophenotypic and metabolic heterogeneity within the ABC compartment in SLE. Subclustering of ABCs revealed three separate and distinct ABC subsets, encompassing CD68 ABCs, NKG7 ABCs, and AREG ABCs, differing in their respecrive transcriptional, functional, and immunometabolic signatures. The CD68 ABC subset demonstrated signs of enhanced cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, lysosomal activity, and increased antigen-processing capabilities. The CD68 and NKG7 ABC populations exhibited increased inflammatory pathway activity, including pattern-recognition receptor signalling and NLRP3 inflammasome-associated activity, while the AREG ABC subset displayed signs of senescence, moderation, exhaustion, or anergy. hdWGCNA identified transcriptional modules associated with acetyltransferase activity, suggesting a potential link between metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodelling through epimetabolite availability, in particular acetyl-CoA. ABCs demonstrated, in general, coordinated amplification of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid utilization, with substantial intragroup metabolic heterogeneity among the three ABC subsets. The CD68 ABCs emerged as the most hypermetabolic subset. In parallel, SCENITH-based metabolic comparison of CD21-CD23- DN B cells between mildly diseased male and severely diseased female MRL.lpr mice revealed increased utilization of alternative non-glucose substrates and enhanced glycolytic activity, but reduced overall protein synthesis capacity, indicating altered allocation of metabolic resources. Further interpretation of the transcriptomic analysis suggests that proteasomal activity could explain the lower protein levels in female MRL.lpr mice, as measured by SCENITH. In addition, in silico drug prediction pointed towards statins and proteasome inhibitors as potentially useful pharmacological agents for blocking cholesterol metabolism and protein degradation, respectively. Finally, the analysis of aged mice also revealed metabolic and redox alterations in ABC-enriched CD21-CD23- DN B cells under physiological aging conditions. Conclusions: Human ABCs appear to comprise a heterogeneous constellation of various subsets possessing different functional properties, as well as different pro-inflammatory or immunoregulatory statuses. ABCs exhibit a distinct hypermetabolic state associated with lupus-related immune dysregulation, but also with aging, in line with previous reports. However, as the disease manifests and progresses, protein production appears to be dampened, which could be attributed to ribosomal problems or proteasome-mediated protein degradation. Metabolic reprogramming is accompanied by enhanced phagocytic and lysosomal programs, which may facilitate the uptake of self-material and contribute to autoreactive immune responses, in particular anti-nuclear autoantibody production. Increased OXPHOS activity may accommodate epigenetic reprogramming towards the atypical memory phenotype displayed by ABCs. Identification of ABC-specific metabolic dependencies may provide opportunities for therapeutic intervention, with lipid consumption being of particular interest. These findings support further investigation of metabolic modulators, including HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and proteasome-targeting strategies, to limit their pathogenic activity in SLE by exploiting their niche metabolic vulnerabilities, in particular their hypermetabolic state and proteostatic stress.

items.title: Cholesterol and high concentration serum cooperatively enhance canine CAR T cell transduction and expansion
items.corresponding_institution: UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Eshelman School of Pharmacy
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell immunotherapy is emerging as a promising adjunct treatment option for refractory canine cancers. Unfortunately, clinical trials thus far have failed to meaningfully reduce tumor burden, highlighting the need for improved CAR T cell manufacturing strategies. Effective autologous therapy requires highly viable, efficiently transduced T cells capable of robust expansion, sustained CAR expression, and long-term persistence. Although these parameters have been extensively investigated in humans, comparable optimization in canine systems remains limited. Here, we evaluated culture conditions to improve canine T cell expansion, memory differentiation, and retroviral transduction efficiency. We demonstrated IL-2 supplementation supported superior cellular expansion and preservation of less-differentiated memory phenotypes compared to IL-7 with IL-15. Additionally, we found that increasing cell density during shorter stimulation periods improved expansion while also driving better T cell transduction rates. We discovered that the addition of cholesterol and high-concentration fetal bovine serum (FBS) to media during the transduction period reliably and markedly enhanced transduction efficiency following a single round of retroviral transduction, even at elevated temperatures that would otherwise impair transduction efficiency. This enhancement was observed with both GALV- and RD114-pseudotyped retroviruses and was accompanied by a marked improvement in cellular expansion without driving terminal differentiation of T cell subsets that are prone to exhaustion in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify practical strategies to improve canine CAR T-cell manufacturing and advance the development of clinically viable CAR T cells for canine cancer treatment.

items.title: Intravenous BCG Elicits a Sustained Myeloid IFNG Response Signature Associated with Early TB Control
items.abstract: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) administered intravenously (IV) to rhesus macaques can prevent pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) infection. To establish transcriptional correlates of protection, we generated longitudinal CITE-Seq data across blood and lung after IV BCG in macaques and compared it to clinically approved intradermal (ID) BCG. We define an interferon gamma (IFNG) response signature in alveolar macrophages (AMs) comprising 61 genes with diverging expression between IV and ID BCG from 4 to 16 weeks after vaccination that was also enriched in AMs early after TB challenge. The signature was recapitulated in blood monocytes (IV vs. ID) and associated with protection in an independent cohort of IV BCG-vaccinated macaques. Cell-cell communication analysis inferred increased ligand-receptor interactions in the airway after IV BCG, including those between multiple IFNG-producing T cell subsets and AMs. The sustained IFNG response signature in AMs after IV BCG provides a new correlate and potential mechanism of early TB control informing future vaccine design.

items.title: Alternative splicing links sex to neutrophil inflammatory vulnerability
items.abstract: Mammalian females generally live longer than males, yet the immunological drivers governing sex-biased inflammatory mortality remain unclear. Neutrophils, among conserved immune cells across species, exhibit marked sex differences in inflammatory and age-related diseases. We identified conserved male-biased CD11b expression in resting neutrophils of wild-type mice, Rag2 KO mice, and in human cohorts. Male neutrophils selectively displayed CD11b-dependent transendothelial migration. During tissue inflammation in our mouse model deficient in -Klotho (Kl) combined with Rag2 KO lymphocyte depletion (dKO), males showed higher mortality and more severe pulmonary pathology correlated with increased infiltrating neutrophils in the lung. The neutrophil accumulation directly accounted for heightened IL-1{beta} expression in males despite equivalent per-cell cytokine expression across sexes. Transcriptomic analysis of neutrophils revealed profound sex-biased alternative splicing enriched in Toll-like receptor (TLR) cascades, alongside hormone-responsive regulation of integrin {beta}2 (Itgb2) isoform usage, implicating alternative splicing in neutrophils represents male vulnerability to tissue inflammation.

items.title: Early Corneal Host-Response Signatures Associate with Disease Severity and Etiology-Related Clinical Outcomes in Fungal Keratitis
items.abstract: Background: To advance host-based predictive marker development for individual risk assessment in fungal keratitis (FK), we investigated corneal host-response gene-expression signatures associated with etiology-related disease course and clinical outcomes. Methods: We compared severity, healing, and visual outcomes in 1,304 patients with Fusarium spp., Aspergillus flavus, or culture-negative keratitis. Presentation-stage corneal scrapings from 70 prospective patients underwent bulk RNA sequencing stratified by etiology, severity, and outcome. Candidate signatures were independently validated by RT-qPCR in 102 patients using clinical correlations, individual cutoff-based profiling, and masked testing, followed by experimental evaluation in corneal epithelial and macrophage-like cells challenged with live fungal spores. Results: Fusarium keratitis more frequently healed with preserved vision. A. flavus and culture-negative keratitis had the highest and lowest proportions of severe and unhealed disease, respectively, despite similarly poor visual outcomes among healed patients. Transcriptomics paralleled these patterns, revealing a distinct Fusarium host response but substantial A. flavus-culture-negative concordance. A coordinated 8-gene innate-response module correlated with ulcer size and discriminated severe from non-severe disease (AUC, 0.82-0.96), while showing more robust expression in A. flavus and culture-negative than Fusarium keratitis. Higher corneal ICOSL was associated with healing, whereas increased SLC26A4/pendrin characterized non-healing and visual impairment, particularly in Fusarium keratitis. Together, these formed a 10-gene panel whose cutoff-based profiles showed concordance with severity and outcome in masked testing. Experimental evaluation revealed cell- and pathogen-specific expression patterns consistent with patient profiles. Conclusions: Presentation-stage corneal host-response profiles capture etiology-associated differences in FK severity and outcome and identify a candidate 10-gene framework for individualized risk stratification.

items.title: H19 isoform switching during neuronal differentiation reveals a distinct pluripotency-associated non-canonical transcript
items.abstract: H19 is one of the earliest discovered and most extensively studied lncRNAs, yet most studies have focused on the canonical 2,315-nt transcript arising from the IGF2/H19 locus on chromosome 11. We examined H19 isoform usage during the pluripotency-to-neuronal transition using NGN2/ASCL1-induced neurogenesis in KOLF2.1J human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). We show that a smaller, non-canonical isoform, variant 3, is the predominant H19 isoform in the pluripotent cells examined. This isoform lacks the large canonical promoter-derived exon 1 and contains a short, unique first exon encoded within the imprinting control region upstream of H19. Upon neuronal induction, isoform-specific RT-qPCR showed that variant 3 declined below the lower limit of reliable quantification (LLRQ) as canonical H19 and IGF2 mRNA increased. In contrast, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells expressed canonical H19, while variant 3 remained below the LLRQ during neurogenic, osteogenic, and adipogenic differentiation. Independent FANTOM5 CAGE datasets supported transcription initiation in the predicted variant 3 promoter region in hiPSCs and human embryonic stem cells. Long-read RNA-seq identified transcripts linking the variant 3 first exon to downstream H19 exons. Public OCT4 and SOX2 ChIP-seq datasets showed recurrent peak overlap at the upstream OSM1 candidate region in pluripotent cells, with corresponding peaks absent in the differentiated datasets examined. Together, these findings support cell-state-associated regulation of the IGF2/H19 locus and identify alternative H19 isoform usage as a feature of human pluripotent cells.

items.title: Human Precision-Cut Kidney Slices as a Translational Platform for Modelling Fibrotic, Inflammatory, Metabolic and Drug-Induced Kidney Injury
items.abstract: Introduction. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterised by progressive fibrosis and inflammation. Preclinical models of these processes translate poorly to human CKD. Animal models are limited by species differences, while two-dimensional cultures and organoids do not reproduce the three-dimensional, multicellular environment of the human kidney. We sought to develop and characterise precision-cut human kidney slices (PCKS) as an ex-vivo platform for studying renal disease and testing therapeutics. Methods. PCKS were prepared from human donor kidneys not utilised for transplantation and cultured in a proprietary bioreactor for up to six days. Tissue integrity, fibrogenesis, inflammation, lipid handling, and drug-induced injury were assessed by histology, digital pathology, secreted protein quantification, mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, and bulk RNA sequencing, with and without pharmacological intervention. Results. PCKS retained native cortical architecture and viability throughout culture. Slices underwent spontaneous, time-dependent fibrogenesis that was enhanced by transforming growth factor beta 1, abrogated by an ALK5 inhibitor, and attenuated by nintedanib but not pirfenidone. Single-fibre digital pathology resolved treatment-dependent changes in collagen content, morphology and architecture. Proinflammatory stimuli induced stimulus-selective cytokine and chemokine secretion through NF-{kappa}B, which was suppressed by an IKK2 inhibitor. Fatty acid treatment reproduced features of fatty kidney disease, including triacylglycerol accumulation and dose-dependent inflammation, while nephrotoxic drugs produced characteristic injury detectable across multiple longitudinal readouts. Conclusions. Human PCKS maintain renal architecture and viability ex-vivo and reproduce fibrotic, inflammatory, metabolic, and toxic responses at transcriptomic, proteomic and lipidomic scales. PCKS provide a physiologically relevant, human-based platform for renal disease modeling and drug discovery.

items.title: Structural basis for m2,2G27 formation and tRNA remodeling by human TRMT1L
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Integrative Biology and Pharmacology, McGovern Medical School, University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, Houston TX USA
items.abstract: tRNAs acquire complex chemical signatures through ordered maturation pathways in which some enzymes contribute both catalytic and non-catalytic activities. Human TRMT1L installs m2,2G27 in tyrosine tRNA and has been reported to support D-loop acp3U20 formation, but the structural basis connecting these functions is unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutagenesis show that TRMT1L is a homodimer that extensively reshapes its tRNA substrate. One protomer clamps the acceptor and T arms and supplies the catalytic pocket, while the other engages the anticodon loop. Charge reversal at these anticodon contacts abolishes methylation without disrupting the dimer, showing that engagement by one protomer is required for catalysis by the other. Cofactor binding is accompanied by reorganization of the D- and anticodon arms that draws G27 into the catalytic pocket. In a second cofactor-bound state an active-site loop (L1) that is disordered without cofactor becomes ordered near the position of the extruded base, suggesting a steric gating mechanism that controls access to the catalytic site. Thus, TRMT1L remodels its substrate rather than closing around it, a property that may explain its requirement for modifications that it does not itself catalyze.

items.title: Publicly Available Genomic Evidence for Nipah and Avian Influenza Viruses in Bangladesh: A Scoping Assessment of Metadata Completeness and Surveillance Representativeness at the Human-Animal Interface
items.abstract: Bangladesh experiences recurrent Nipah virus (NiV) outbreaks and sustained avian influenza virus (AIV) activity. Whether public genomic records contain metadata needed to assess surveillance representativeness across hosts, locations, and time is unclear.We conducted a structured, source-based scoping assessment of publicly documented NiV and AIV genomic records from Bangladesh (2001-2025), drawing on NCBI GenBank/INSDC and cited peer-reviewed and public-health sources. A pilot registry contained 108 entries (55 NiV, 53 AIV). Metadata were retained only when explicitly reported; unverified fields were recorded as not extracted. The registry is not a complete census. Five analytical questions were prespecified; several could not be evaluated because accession-level metadata were unavailable. The 33-accession AIV set containing H5N1 and H3N8 was excluded from H5/H9-specific interpretation. In the pilot registry, 9/108 entries (8.3%) had explicitly reported host species; the separate host-implied category was not added. Twelve entries (11.1%) had a full collection date; 21 (19.4%) had any collection date. Eight entries (7.4%) had an explicit district. The registry lists 22 NiV accession identifiers from a 2026 study, whereas the publication reports 23 newly sequenced N-gene records; this remains unresolved. Eight AIV accessions (PV961349.1-PV961356.1) represent eight segments of one chicken H5N1 isolate, not eight genomes. Twelve MN994-series records are HA-gene sequences from environmental live-bird-market samples.The pilot registry demonstrates substantial metadata limitations. Explicit host information was available for 8.3% of entries and explicit district for 7.4%; these prevent reliable quantitative assessment of host, district-level, and temporal representativeness and do not establish absence of surveillance or viral circulation. Accession-level reconstruction with transparent verification tiers and harmonised identifiers is required before quantitative representativeness indices or district-level priorities can be calculated.

items.title: RepeatViewer: a platform for explorative analysis of repetitive DNAs
items.abstract: RepeatViewer is a graphical user interface application designed for repetitive sequence inspection and curation, especially focusing on, but not limited to, transposable elements (TEs). It automatically identifies structural features of TEs, including long terminal repeats (LTRs), terminal inverted repeats (TIRs), and target side duplications (TSDs). All detected and user-defined annotations can be interactively inspected, edited, and exported. RepeatViewer also integrates a TE curation workflow intended to facilitate their manual refinement. In addition, it provides interactive visualization of TE sequences and genome-wide TE annotations, such as dot plots as well as TE distribution and divergence analyses. RepeatViewer is modularly built and can be easily customized by the user.

items.title: ONTOLOGY™: Streamlined DNA Barcoding and Metabarcoding on Nanopore
items.corresponding_institution: Centre for Biodiversity Genomics, University of Guelph
items.abstract: Nanopore sequencers have unlocked the potential for a distributed network of DNA barcoding and metabarcoding laboratories. However, the realization of this potential confronts two challenges--one molecular, one computational. First, rigorous indexing protocols are critical to correctly associate sequences with their source specimen or sample; and second, data interpretation often demands processing millions of indexed reads in a structured fashion via complex bioinformatic pipelines. ONTOLOGY addresses these challenges. At its core lies a graphical user interface (GUI) that guides users through the workflow from specimen or sample reception to the generation of DNA barcode records or metabarcode files. To facilitate data acquisition, it includes freeze-dried PCR plates that uniquely tag the amplicons from each well, hence supporting sample-sequence association. The ONTOLOGY GUI is constructed around two core workflows that process data from a sequencing Run. The Barcode Inference Pipeline (BIP) delineates the OTU(s) recovered from each well and designates them as target or non-target sequences via comparison of OTU sequences to a reference sequence library. The Metabarcoding Analysis Pipeline (MAP) processes sequence arrays derived from bulk samples (organismal or environmental DNA) and infers the species represented while rigorously excluding false positives. To validate ONTOLOGY, we present an original data analysis completed via both pipelines. Built for maximum flexibility, ONTOLOGY also supports the analysis of custom experiments. By employing a GUI to coordinate passage through the workflows with structured amplicon tagging and informatics pipelines, ONTOLOGY facilitates the molecular analyses needed to advance biodiversity science via decentralization. Plates and software can be obtained from www.ontology.bio.

items.title: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
items.abstract: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence. Pretrained on 32.4 million RNA sequences, RIPPLE uses pairwise predictive utility to guide relational learning, transferring training-time supervision into a sequence-only model without requiring structural inputs at inference. RIPPLE improves overall performance across five downstream tasks spanning RNA family classification, ribosome loading prediction, secondary-structure prediction, three-dimensional contact prediction, and splice-site recognition. Mechanistic analyses further show that utility-guided learning improves the recovery of informative interactions and enhances the transferability of learned RNA representations.

items.title: gPlace: fast, memory-bounded phylogenetic placement with results identical to pplacer
items.abstract: Phylogenetic placement methods such as pplacer attach query sequences to a fixed reference tree, thereby establishing their evolutionary relationships to the reference sequences. These relationships can then be used to infer taxonomic classifications or likely metabolic functions. gPlace is a drop-in replacement for pplacer that produces identical results while reducing memory requirements by >3-fold and computation time by >30-fold under typical usage. These improvements are achieved by storing less data per node and streamlining the calculations used to position each query sequence. gPlace can also run within a user-specified memory limit by processing only a portion of the reference tree at a time. Consequently, it can efficiently place sequences on large reference trees that would be impractical for pplacer to process. We demonstrate the importance of these improvements by evaluating gPlace as a replacement for pplacer in GTDB-Tk and CheckM, two tools widely used in genome-resolved metagenomic studies. gPlace is released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 and is available at https://github.com/cmc-aau/gPlace.

items.title: Cell-type label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims in spatial transcriptomics
items.abstract: Niche analyses ask how a cell's neighbors shape its expression beyond its type. The type comes from a label, and labels are imperfect. Here we show that label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims. A mislabeled cell still expresses its true type, and because cells of a type sit near one another, the neighborhood is credited with what the label misses. Standard practice, which calls labels on the modeled counts and selects cells by them, hid, exaggerated, or reversed this inflation. Labeling one half of each cell's counts and modeling the other revealed it in nearly every population of six datasets. On semi-synthetic colon data, a labeler that over-called one fibroblast subtype reversed claims of the niche method Niche-DE; new draws of the counts and errors spread at random over subtypes almost never did. Our software, nichepeek, reports the direction of this bias in a user's data.

items.title: Substrate rigidity suppresses the NRF2 antioxidant program in breast cancer cells
items.abstract: Matrix stiffness rises as breast tumors progress, but whether rigidity raises or lowers activity of the KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway is contested: work in breast cancer cells places the antioxidant response on soft matrix, while work in liver cancer places response on stiff. We used publicly available transcriptome data to ask the question across laboratories rather than within one system. Of eleven series identified, four dataset arms passed quality criteria fixed before any biological analysis. Across five contrasts spanning three cell lines and two matrix formats, one program responded in the same direction every time: the NRF2 antioxidant battery was lower on the more rigid substrate in all five. In contrast, SLC7A11, the cystine transporter supporting glutathione synthesis, decreased in all five, by up to 6.5-fold. YAP and TEAD targets did not track rigidity, rising on hydrogels and glass but falling on cell-derived matrix. NFE2L2 and its regulators were unchanged, while targets fell in proportion to their dependence on the antioxidant response element, pointing to control after transcription. An unsupervised partition made without reference to any pathway recovered the same program and survived removal of proliferation genes. In 1,097 TCGA and 1,980 METABRIC breast tumors, the matrix proxy was unrelated to the full battery until immune and hypoxic composition were accounted for, after which the same negative direction appeared in both; and a tumor-intrinsic score excluding macrophage-expressed members showed it more directly. Single-cell and spatial tests produced the predicted direction but could not resolve it, due to limited sample size and because the genes carrying the effect are largely undetectable at spot depth. Reduced antioxidant capacity on rigid substrate predicts greater sensitivity to agents killing through lipid peroxidation, a prediction we set out for experimental test.
